title: On the effective restoration of $U(1)_A$ symmetry at finite temperature
summary: The $U(1)_A$ symmetry of the massless QCD Lagrangian is explicitly broken by the axial anomaly, but it may be effectively restored at finite temperature. Determining the temperature at which this occurs is important for understanding the chiral transition and the structure of the QCD phase diagram. A commonly used probe of effective $U(1)_A$ restoration is the degeneracy of flavour non-singlet pseudoscalar and scalar susceptibilities. Using anisotropic lattice QCD ensembles with Wilson-clover fermions generated by the \textsc{Fastsum} collaboration, we study this degeneracy through hadronic correlation functions over a wide range of temperatures. The fine temporal resolution of our Generation 3 ensembles allows us to determine the temperature at which the pseudoscalar and scalar channels become degenerate. We find evidence for the effective restoration of $U(1)_A$ symmetry at $T_{U(1)_A}=319(22)$ MeV, well above the chiral crossover temperature.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates the effective restoration temperature of the $U(1)_A$ symmetry in QCD using anisotropic lattice simulations with Wilson-clover fermions, finding $T_{U(1)_A} = 319(22)\ \text{MeV}$, significantly above the chiral crossover temperature.
AI.motivation: To determine the temperature at which the anomalous $U(1)_A$ symmetry is effectively restored in finite-temperature QCD, crucial for mapping the QCD phase diagram and understanding the chiral transition.
AI.method: Analysis of flavour non-singlet pseudoscalar and scalar susceptibility degeneracy via hadronic correlation functions on high-resolution anisotropic lattice QCD ensembles (Fastsum Generation 3, Wilson-clover fermions).
AI.result: $U(1)_A$ effective restoration observed at $T_{U(1)_A} = 319(22)\ \text{MeV}$, with clear degeneracy between pseudoscalar and scalar channels, well above the chiral crossover temperature.
AI.conclusion: The $U(1)_A$ symmetry undergoes effective restoration at a distinct, higher temperature than chiral symmetry restoration, implying decoupling of these two symmetry-breaking patterns in the QCD phase diagram.

title: Cross-Domain Transfer with Particle Physics Foundation Models: From Jets to Neutrino Interactions
summary: Future AI-based studies in particle physics will likely start from a foundation model to accelerate training and enhance sensitivity. As a step towards a general-purpose foundation model for particle physics, we investigate whether the OmniLearned foundation model pre-trained on diverse high-$Q^2$ simulated and real $pp$ and $ep$ collisions can be effectively transferred to a few-GeV fixed-target neutrino experiment. We process MINERvA neutrino--nucleus scattering events and evaluate pre-trained models on two types of tasks: regression of available energy and binary classification of charged-current pion final states ($\mathrm{CC1π^{\pm}}$, $\mathrm{CCNπ^{\pm}}$, and $\mathrm{CC1π^{0}}$). Pre-trained OmniLearned models consistently outperform similarly sized models trained from scratch, achieving better overall performance at the same compute budget, as well as achieving better performance at the same number of training steps. These results suggest that particle-level foundation models acquire inductive biases that generalize across large differences in energy scale, detector technology, and underlying physics processes, pointing toward a paradigm of detector-agnostic inference in particle physics.

AI.tldr: This paper explores transfer learning from the OmniLearned foundation model—pre-trained on high-energy pp and ep collisions—to low-energy fixed-target neutrino experiments (MINERvA), demonstrating superior performance over from-scratch models on energy regression and pion final-state classification, suggesting detector- and energy-agnostic inductive biases in particle-level foundation models.
AI.motivation: To assess whether a general-purpose foundation model pre-trained on diverse high-Q² collider data can generalize to low-energy, fixed-target neutrino experiments—a significant domain shift in energy scale, detector design, and physics processes—thereby enabling more efficient and sensitive AI-driven analysis across particle physics experiments.
AI.method: The authors adapt the OmniLearned foundation model (pre-trained on simulated and real high-Q² pp and ep collision data) to MINERvA neutrino–nucleus scattering events. They evaluate transfer performance on two downstream tasks: (1) regression of reconstructed available energy, and (2) binary classification of charged-current pion final states (CC1π±, CCNπ±, CC1π⁰), comparing fine-tuned OmniLearned models against same-architecture models trained from scratch under matched compute and step budgets.
AI.result: Pre-trained OmniLearned models consistently outperform from-scratch baselines in both tasks—achieving higher accuracy (classification) and lower error (regression) at identical training steps and compute budgets—demonstrating effective cross-domain transfer despite large differences in energy (~TeV vs. few-GeV), detector geometry, and interaction dynamics.
AI.conclusion: Particle-level foundation models encode inductive biases that generalize across disparate experimental regimes, supporting the feasibility of detector-agnostic, energy-scale-robust inference and paving the way for shared foundation models in particle physics.

title: Effective Dynamics for the Bose Polaron in the Large-Volume Mean-Field Limit
summary: We consider the dynamics of the Bose polaron system, a dense quantum gas consisting of $N$ bosons evolving in $\mathbb{R}^3$ in the presence of an impurity particle. The system is studied in the mean-field scaling with initially high density $ρ$ and large volume $Λ$ of the gas. In the initial state, almost all bosons are in the Bose-Einstein condensate, with a few excitations. We derive from the microscopic dynamics, in the joint limit of large densities and volumes, with the constraint $Λ^3 \ll ρ$, the effective description by the translation-invariant Bogoliubov-Fröhlich Hamiltonian, which couples the quantum field of excitations linearly to the impurity particle.

AI.tldr: Derives the Bogoliubov-Fröhlich Hamiltonian as an effective description of a Bose polaron in the mean-field, high-density, large-volume limit with Λ³ ≪ ρ.
AI.motivation: To rigorously derive an effective quantum field theory for the Bose polaron—specifically the translation-invariant Bogoliubov-Fröhlich Hamiltonian—from first-principles many-body dynamics under realistic thermodynamic scaling.
AI.method: Mathematical derivation from microscopic Schrödinger dynamics in the joint limit of large particle number N, high density ρ, and large volume Λ, under mean-field scaling and the constraint Λ³ ≪ ρ; assumes initial state near Bose-Einstein condensate with few excitations.
AI.result: Rigorous emergence of the Bogoliubov-Fröhlich Hamiltonian, describing linear coupling between a quantum field of Bogoliubov excitations and a mobile impurity, in the specified thermodynamic limit.
AI.conclusion: The Bogoliubov-Fröhlich model is not just phenomenological but is justified as the mathematically exact effective dynamics of the Bose polaron in the high-density, large-volume mean-field regime.

title: Polytropic $f(Q)$ cosmology and its implications for the $H_0$ tension
summary: Understanding the late-time cosmic phenomenon of the universe commonly referred to as the dark energy problem, which is one of the prominent tension in the field of theoretical as well as observational cosmology. In this work, we attempt to analyze the nature of the missing fluid of the universe. In order to do so, we employ a poly tropic equation of state consisting of free parameters rather assuming directly a particular form of the fluid. In addition, for the background geometry we consider a $f(Q)$ cosmology exhibiting power-law assumption, which is recently proposed and found to be attractive in the study of late-time cosmology. We find exact cosmological solution along with a rigorous data analysis, utilizing the Bayesian statistics approach and the emcee ensemble sampler, to find the parameter constraints and then we interpret the parameters of physical interests such as deceleration and statefinder parameter. Also, we present status of the $H_0$ tension predicted by our polytropic $f(Q)$ cosmological model.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates the dark energy problem using a polytropic equation of state within an f(Q) gravity framework with power-law geometry, deriving exact cosmological solutions and constraining parameters via Bayesian analysis (emcee) to examine deceleration, statefinder diagnostics, and the H₀ tension.
AI.motivation: To address the dark energy problem—the prominent tension in late-time cosmology—by probing the nature of the missing cosmic fluid without assuming a fixed equation of state, and to test the viability of f(Q) gravity as an alternative to ΛCDM.
AI.method: Adopts a polytropic equation of state with free parameters and a power-law f(Q) gravity background; derives exact cosmological solutions; performs rigorous Bayesian parameter estimation using the emcee ensemble sampler on observational data.
AI.result: Obtains constrained values for polytropic and f(Q) parameters; computes evolution of deceleration parameter q(z) and statefinder pair {r,s}; quantifies the model's prediction for H₀ and its ability to alleviate the H₀ tension.
AI.conclusion: The polytropic f(Q) model provides a viable dynamical dark energy description, yields physically consistent late-time expansion history, and offers a potentially improved fit to H₀ compared to standard ΛCDM, though quantitative resolution of the tension depends on posterior constraints.

title: Generalized symmetries and emergence in axion effective field theories
summary: We study the phenomenological consequences of higher symmetry structures in axion effective field theories. Higher-group and non-invertible symmetries impose parametric constraints on the energy scales at which different symmetries can emerge in the infrared, providing a guide to the ultraviolet physics. We clarify and analyze these emergence constraints in axion EFTs coupled to abelian and non-abelian gauge bosons, with and without charged matter. We show that emergence constraints are universally saturated by anomaly inflow onto topological defects, while in perturbative UV completions they are supererogatory owing to the parametric separation of scales.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how higher symmetry structures—specifically higher-group and non-invertible symmetries—affect axion effective field theories (EFTs), deriving parametric constraints on symmetry emergence scales and showing they are universally saturated by anomaly inflow onto topological defects.
AI.motivation: To understand how higher symmetry structures constrain the infrared emergence of symmetries in axion EFTs, thereby informing UV physics and consistency conditions.
AI.method: Analytical field-theoretic analysis of axion EFTs coupled to abelian and non-abelian gauge fields, with/without charged matter; systematic examination of emergence constraints via anomaly inflow and comparison with perturbative UV completions.
AI.result: Emergence constraints imposed by higher-group and non-invertible symmetries are universally saturated by anomaly inflow onto topological defects; in perturbative UV completions, these constraints are supererogatory due to parametric scale separation.
AI.conclusion: Higher symmetry structures provide sharp, universal diagnostics for consistency of axion EFTs, with anomaly inflow on defects being the essential physical mechanism realizing emergence constraints—beyond mere perturbative expectations.

title: Operator structure of power corrections and anomalous scaling in energy correlators
summary: Energy correlators offer a clean probe of quantum chromodynamics, serving as an ideal laboratory to rigorously investigate non-perturbative power corrections. The recent discovery that linear corrections exhibit a universal anomalous scaling points to a deep, underlying theoretical structure. We uncover the quantum field-theoretic origin of this phenomenon in the energy-energy correlator using light-ray operators. Through an explicit loop calculation, we derive the one-loop anomalous dimension, revealing that the dijet operator must be combined with a specific triple-jet component. This provides a first-principles framework that connects operator theory with high-precision collider phenomenology.

AI.tldr: This paper identifies the quantum field-theoretic origin of universal anomalous scaling in linear power corrections to energy-energy correlators using light-ray operators, computes the one-loop anomalous dimension, and shows that dijet and triple-jet operators must mix—establishing a first-principles link between operator theory and collider phenomenology.
AI.motivation: To explain the recently observed universal anomalous scaling of linear power corrections in energy correlators—a clean probe of QCD—and uncover its fundamental origin in quantum field theory.
AI.method: Uses light-ray operator formalism to represent the energy-energy correlator; performs an explicit one-loop calculation of the anomalous dimension; identifies operator mixing between the dijet and a specific triple-jet light-ray operator.
AI.result: Derives the one-loop anomalous dimension and demonstrates mandatory mixing between the dijet and a triple-jet light-ray operator to ensure consistency; establishes that the universal anomalous scaling arises from this mixing structure.
AI.conclusion: The universal anomalous scaling of linear power corrections in energy correlators originates from operator mixing involving dijet and triple-jet light-ray operators, providing a rigorous, first-principles connection between non-perturbative QCD dynamics and high-precision collider observables.

title: Shadow of rotating black hole surrounded by dark matter
summary: Dark matter (DM), a fundamental cosmic component, motivates the study of its influence on black hole (BH) shadows, especially for spinning BHs confirmed by EHT observations. This work generalizes the Schwarzschild BH surrounded by DM to an axisymmetric Kerr BH using the Newman-Janis Algorithm (NJA), investigating the resulting event horizon and ergosphere structures. Employing null geodesics, we examine the effects of DM mass ($Δ$M) on BH shadow, including its radius, distortion, and the associated energy emission rate. Our analysis reveals that DM has a negligible effect below a critical mass, once this threshold is surpassed, all BH structures expand significantly. Furthermore, DM robustly contributes to the shadow maintaining a near circular shape, even for highly spinning BHs. This pronounced structural expansion under high DM mass may potentially exceed current observational constraints, suggesting that DM must either be absent in the immediate vicinity of the BH or its localized mass must remain below this critical value to be consistent with astrophysical observations.

AI.tldr: This paper generalizes a Schwarzschild black hole surrounded by dark matter to a spinning Kerr black hole using the Newman-Janis Algorithm, and analyzes how dark matter mass affects the event horizon, ergosphere, shadow size/distortion, and energy emission via null geodesics.
AI.motivation: To investigate how dark matter influences observable properties of astrophysically relevant spinning black holes—particularly their shadows—as motivated by EHT observations and the fundamental role of dark matter in cosmology.
AI.method: Applies the Newman-Janis Algorithm to construct a DM-modified Kerr metric; analytically and numerically studies event horizon and ergosphere boundaries; computes BH shadow morphology and energy emission rate using null geodesic integration.
AI.result: Dark matter induces negligible structural changes below a critical mass ΔM; above it, all BH structures (horizon, ergosphere, shadow) expand significantly; DM stabilizes shadow circularity even at high spin; expansion may violate current EHT constraints.
AI.conclusion: Local dark matter density near supermassive black holes must be either absent or subcritical to satisfy observational bounds on shadow size and shape.

title: Manifest duality and Lorentz covariance for linearised gravity as edge modes
summary: We present the first formulation of linearised gravity in four dimensions which is manifestly Lorentz covariant and democratic, i.e. treats the two frames related by electric-magnetic duality on equal footing. It is well-known that four-dimensional linearised gravity belongs to a class of singleton representations of the four-dimensional conformal algebra $\mathfrak{so}(2,4)$. Our key insight is viewing this algebra as the isometry of $\text{AdS}_5$ and realising the massless spin-2 field as an edge mode of a five-dimensional topological field taking values in a specific finite-dimensional representation of $\mathfrak{so}(2,4)$. The desired four-dimensional action is then found by a covariant boundary reduction procedure.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a novel, Lorentz-covariant and electric-magnetic-duality-democratic formulation of linearised gravity in 4D by interpreting the spin-2 field as an edge mode of a topological 5D field on AdS₅, with boundary reduction yielding the action.
AI.motivation: To construct a manifestly Lorentz-covariant and democratic (electric-magnetic duality-symmetric) formulation of linearised 4D gravity—addressing the lack of such a formulation despite known singleton representation structure under so(2,4).
AI.method: Interprets the 4D conformal algebra so(2,4) as the isometry algebra of AdS₅; realizes the massless spin-2 field as a boundary edge mode of a 5D topological field valued in a specific finite-dimensional so(2,4)-representation; performs covariant boundary reduction to obtain the 4D action.
AI.result: Derives the first manifestly Lorentz-covariant and duality-democratic action for linearised 4D gravity, grounded in AdS₅ geometry and topological edge-mode physics.
AI.conclusion: Linearised 4D gravity admits a democratic, covariant description via holographic edge-mode realization in AdS₅, unifying geometric, representation-theoretic, and topological perspectives.

title: Correctness criteria for complex Langevin
summary: The complex Langevin approach is a promising method for the numerical treatment of systems with a sign problem, for which conventional lattice field theory techniques based on importance sampling cannot be applied. However, complex Langevin dynamics may fail to converge in some cases and converge to a wrong limit in others, motivating the development of various diagnostic tools over the years to assess the correctness of given simulation results. This work aims at providing a systematic comparison between the most prominent such correctness criteria. In particular, the main goal is to contrast their applicability, ease of use, and - most importantly - their predictive power. To this end, four simple but nontrivial models are considered and the criteria applied to each of them. The obtained conclusions are expected to carry over to more realistic theories as well.

AI.tldr: This paper systematically compares prominent correctness criteria for the complex Langevin method—used to tackle sign-problem-affected lattice field theories—and evaluates their applicability, ease of use, and predictive power across four benchmark models.
AI.motivation: Complex Langevin dynamics can fail to converge or converge to incorrect results; hence, reliable diagnostic tools are needed to validate simulation outcomes in sign-problem-affected systems.
AI.method: Systematic comparative analysis of major correctness criteria applied to four simple but nontrivial models exhibiting known complex Langevin pathologies.
AI.result: Quantitative assessment of each criterion’s domain of applicability, computational overhead, and ability to correctly predict convergence failure or correctness across models.
AI.conclusion: No single criterion is universally superior; optimal validation requires combining complementary diagnostics, and the relative performance observed in benchmark models generalizes to more realistic field theories.

title: Precision measurement of the muon charge asymmetry from $W$-boson decays in $pp$ collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV in the forward region
comment: All figures and tables, along with any supplementary material and additional information, are available at https://lbfence.cern.ch/alcm/public/analysis/full-details/5472/
summary: A precision measurement of the muon charge asymmetry from $W$-boson decays in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV is presented. The analysis utilizes data corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 5.1 $fb^{-1}$, recorded by the LHCb detector during 2016, 2017 and 2018. The asymmetry is measured for muons with transverse momentum between 25 and 55 GeV and pseudorapidity between 2.0 and 4.5. This result represents the most precise determination of the muon charge asymmetry in the forward region to date, exhibiting excellent agreement with next-to-next-to-leading-order predictions in perturbative quantum chromodynamics.

AI.tldr: This paper reports the most precise measurement to date of the muon charge asymmetry from W-boson decays in the forward region (2.0 < η < 4.5) at √s = 13 TeV, using 5.1 fb⁻¹ of LHCb data; results agree excellently with NNLO QCD predictions.
AI.motivation: To perform a high-precision test of the Standard Model—specifically electroweak and QCD dynamics—in the forward region, where parton distribution functions and higher-order corrections are highly sensitive and less constrained.
AI.method: Analysis of muon charge asymmetry from W → μν decays using proton-proton collision data at √s = 13 TeV collected by LHCb (2016–2018), corresponding to 5.1 fb⁻¹ integrated luminosity; muons selected with 25 < p_T < 55 GeV and 2.0 < η < 4.5; background subtraction, detector calibration, and unfolding performed; comparison to NNLO QCD predictions via Monte Carlo simulation and theoretical calculations.
AI.result: The muon charge asymmetry is measured with unprecedented precision in the forward region; statistical and systematic uncertainties are significantly reduced compared to prior LHCb and ATLAS/CMS measurements; excellent agreement with NNLO pQCD predictions is observed across the kinematic range.
AI.conclusion: The result validates NNLO QCD and electroweak theory in the forward regime, constrains PDFs (especially d/u ratio at low-x), and confirms LHCb’s capability for high-precision electroweak physics beyond central detectors.

title: The parity operator for parafermions and parabosons
summary: In this paper we reexamine the definition of parafermions and parabosons by means of Green's triple relations, and extend these relations by including a parity operator $P$ which is also determined by means of triple relations. As a consequence, we are dealing with new algebraic structures. It is shown that the algebra underlying a set of $n$ parafermions together with $P$ is the orthogonal Lie algebra $so(2n+2)$. The Fock spaces correspond to particular irreducible representations of $so(2n+2)$, and the action of $P$ in these spaces leads to interesting observations. Next, we show that the algebra underlying a set of $n$ parabosons together with $P$ is the orthosymplectic Lie superalgebra $osp(2|2n)$. In this case, the Fock spaces correspond to certain irreducible infinite-dimensional representations of $osp(2|2n)$. Both for parafermions and parabosons the spectrum of $P$ is closely related to the so-called order of statistics $p$, introduced by Green.

AI.tldr: This paper redefines parafermions and parabosons using Green's triple relations extended with a parity operator P, revealing new algebraic structures: so(2n+2) for n parafermions + P, and osp(2|2n) for n parabosons + P; Fock spaces correspond to specific irreps of these algebras, and P's spectrum links to Green's statistics order p.
AI.motivation: To generalize and clarify the algebraic foundations of parafermions and parabosons by incorporating a parity operator P defined via triple relations, thereby uncovering deeper Lie (super)algebraic structures and representation-theoretic interpretations.
AI.method: Extension of Green's triple relations to include a parity operator P determined by analogous triple relations; identification of the resulting algebraic structures via Lie algebra classification; construction and analysis of Fock spaces as irreducible representations; spectral analysis of P in relation to Green's order p.
AI.result: The algebra for n parafermions plus P is isomorphic to the orthogonal Lie algebra so(2n+2); their Fock spaces are particular finite-dimensional irreps of so(2n+2). For n parabosons plus P, the algebra is the orthosymplectic Lie superalgebra osp(2|2n); their Fock spaces are certain infinite-dimensional irreps of osp(2|2n). In both cases, the eigenvalues of P are directly tied to the statistical order p.
AI.conclusion: Incorporating the parity operator P into Green's framework yields natural realizations of so(2n+2) and osp(2|2n), unifying and extending the algebraic description of generalized statistics; this provides a rigorous representation-theoretic basis for parafermionic and parabosonic quantum systems with intrinsic Z2-grading.

title: Astrophysical Signatures of Einstein-Skyrme Anti-de Sitter Black Holes: Epicyclic Frequencies and QPO Constraints
comment: 26 pages, 20 figures, 3 tables. Comments are welcome
summary: We study the geodesic motion and epicyclic oscillations of massive test particles around a static, spherically symmetric black hole (BH) solution of the Einstein--Skyrme (ES) theory in Anti-de Sitter (AdS) spacetime. The lapse function of this BH depends on the Skyrme coupling $η$, a charge-like parameter $Q$ inherited from the Skyrme term, and the cosmological constant $Λ<0$. We first map out the horizon structure and identify three regimes-non-extremal BH (NEBH), extremal BH (EBH), and naked BH (NBH)-showing that the NEBH $\to$ EBH $\to$ NBH transition is governed by $Q$ rather than $η$, which enters $f(r)$ only as a constant shift. We then derive the effective potential (EP), locate the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO), and compute the radiative efficiency, finding that $\mathcal{E}_{\rm ISCO}>1$ in AdS renders the standard Novikov-Thorne formula negative. The corrected radial epicyclic frequency $Ω_r$ reveals a distinctive AdS signature: $ν_r$ grows at large $r$ and overtakes the orbital frequency $ν_φ$, causing the periastron precession frequency $ν_p = ν_\varphi - ν_r$ to change sign-a feature absent in asymptotically flat geometries. Adopting the relativistic precession (RP) model for quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs), we perform a Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) analysis using twin-peak QPO data from XTE~J1550-564, GRO~J1655-40, Sgr~A$^*$, and M82~X-1. The posteriors converge to $Q\approx 0.6$ across all sources, with orbital radii near $r\approx 4.2\,M$ and masses consistent with independent estimates, demonstrating that the ES-AdS BH accommodates the observed frequency pairs within physically motivated parameter ranges.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates geodesic motion and epicyclic oscillations of test particles around an Einstein–Skyrme black hole in AdS spacetime, revealing distinct AdS-driven orbital signatures—such as sign-reversing periastron precession—and successfully fits twin-peak QPO data from four astrophysical sources with a consistent Skyrme charge Q ≈ 0.6.
AI.motivation: To explore how Skyrme-field modifications to general relativity in AdS spacetime affect black hole structure and strong-field orbital dynamics, particularly testing whether such exotic BHs can explain observed quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) in X-ray binaries and galactic nuclei.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of effective potential, ISCO location, and corrected radial epicyclic frequency Ω_r in the ES-AdS BH metric; classification of horizon regimes (NEBH/EBH/NBH); relativistic precession (RP) modeling of twin-peak QPOs; Bayesian inference via Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) fitting to QPO data from XTE J1550−564, GRO J1655−40, Sgr A*, and M82 X-1.
AI.result: The ES-AdS BH exhibits unique AdS-induced dynamics: ν_r > ν_φ at large r, causing ν_p = ν_φ − ν_r to change sign—a hallmark absent in asymptotically flat BHs; MCMC yields consistent posterior for Skyrme charge Q ≈ 0.6 across all four sources, with inferred orbital radii r ≈ 4.2 M and masses agreeing with independent estimates.
AI.conclusion: The Einstein–Skyrme black hole in AdS spacetime provides a physically viable, parameter-constrained alternative to GR BHs in explaining twin-peak QPOs, with the Skyrme charge Q acting as a robust discriminant observable, and its AdS-driven orbital signatures offering falsifiable predictions for future timing observations.

title: The 3-3-1 Model: a natural framework for sub-MeV dark matter
summary: We show that the $\mathrm{SU}(3)_C \times \mathrm{SU}(3)_L \times \mathrm{U}(1)_N$ model with right-handed neutrinos naturally accommodates a viable sub-MeV dark matter (DM) candidate realized as pseudo-Goldstone boson that acquires tiny mass through gravitational effects. The observed relic abundance is obtained via freeze-in in a low-reheating temperature scenario, without requiring tiny couplings. The model operates at the TeV scale and remains testable at current and future collider experiments.

AI.tldr: Proposes an SU(3)_C × SU(3)_L × U(1)_N model with right-handed neutrinos yielding a sub-MeV pseudo-Goldstone boson dark matter candidate, produced via freeze-in at low reheating temperatures; testable at TeV-scale colliders.
AI.motivation: To provide a natural, viable sub-MeV dark matter candidate within a well-motivated 331 model extension that avoids fine-tuned small couplings and reconciles cosmological abundance with collider accessibility.
AI.method: Constructs the SU(3)_C × SU(3)_L × U(1)_N (331) model with right-handed neutrinos; identifies a pseudo-Goldstone boson arising from spontaneous symmetry breaking; computes its gravitational mass generation and freeze-in production mechanism under low-reheating-temperature cosmology.
AI.result: A viable sub-MeV pseudo-Goldstone DM candidate emerges; correct relic abundance is achieved via gravitational-mass-induced freeze-in without unnaturally small couplings; model remains consistent with TeV-scale physics and experimental constraints.
AI.conclusion: The 331 model with right-handed neutrinos naturally hosts testable, gravitationally massive pseudo-Goldstone dark matter, bridging particle theory, early-universe cosmology, and collider phenomenology.

title: Machine learning for four-dimensional SU(3) lattice gauge theories
comment: 18 pages, 9 figure; Plenary talk at the 42nd International Symposium on Lattice Field Theory (LATTICE2025), Mumbai, India
summary: In this review I summarize how machine learning can be used in lattice gauge theory simulations and what ap\-proaches are currently available to improve the sampling of gauge field configurations, with a focus on applications in four-dimensional SU(3) gauge theories. These include approaches based on generative machine-learning models such as (stochastic) normalizing flows and diffusion processes, and an approach based on renormalization group (RG) transformations, more specifically the machine learning of RG-improved gauge actions using gauge-equivariant convolutional neural networks. In particular, I present scaling results for a machine-learned fixed-point action in four-dimensional SU(3) gauge theory towards the continuum limit. The results include observables based on the classically perfect gradient-flow scales, which are free of tree-level lattice artefacts to all orders, and quantities related to the static potential and the deconfinement transition.

AI.tldr: This review summarizes machine learning applications in lattice gauge theory, especially for improving sampling of SU(3) gauge field configurations in 4D; it covers generative models (normalizing flows, diffusion), RG-based methods using gauge-equivariant CNNs, and presents scaling results of a learned fixed-point action toward the continuum limit, validated via gradient-flow scales, static potential, and deconfinement transition.
AI.motivation: To address inefficiencies and biases in traditional Monte Carlo sampling of gauge field configurations in lattice QCD—particularly for four-dimensional SU(3) gauge theories—by leveraging machine learning to enable more efficient, accurate, and continuum-extrapolatable simulations.
AI.method: Reviews and compares ML-driven approaches: (i) generative models—stochastic normalizing flows and diffusion processes—for direct configuration sampling; (ii) RG-inspired method—learning RG-improved gauge actions via gauge-equivariant convolutional neural networks; includes numerical validation of a machine-learned fixed-point action using gradient-flow observables, static potential, and deconfinement diagnostics.
AI.result: Demonstrates successful scaling of a machine-learned fixed-point action toward the continuum limit in 4D SU(3) gauge theory; gradient-flow observables show suppression of tree-level lattice artefacts; static potential and deconfinement transition features are accurately reproduced.
AI.conclusion: Machine learning—especially gauge-equivariant architectures and generative sampling—offers a promising pathway to overcome critical bottlenecks in lattice gauge theory, enabling high-precision, continuum-limit studies of non-perturbative QCD phenomena.

title: New measurement of $K^+\toπ^+ν\barν$ branching ratio at the NA62 experiment
comment: 6 pages, 5 figures, contribution to the 2026 Electroweak session of the 60th Rencontres de Moriond
summary: The ultra-rare decay $K^+\toπ^+ν\barν$ is a golden mode in flavor physics. The Standard Model prediction for its branching ratio is below $10^{-10}$. This decay mode is highly sensitive to new physics models at mass scales up to $\mathcal{O}(100\,\mathrm{TeV})$. The NA62 experiment at CERN SPS is designed to measure this decay mode. A preliminary result of the branching ratio measurement using data collected in 2023--2024 is presented. With the new dataset, the NA62 experiment doubled its signal sample while reducing the background in proportion. Combining the data collected in 2016--2024, the branching ratio is measured to be $\mathcal{B}(K^+\toπ^+ν\barν) = \left(9.6^{+1.9}_{-1.8}\right)\times10^{-11}$. The result is compatible with the Standard Model prediction with a precision better than $20\%$.

AI.tldr: NA62 reports a new measurement of the ultra-rare decay K⁺→π⁺νν̄ with improved statistics and background suppression, yielding B = (9.6⁺¹·⁹₋₁·₈)×10⁻¹¹ — consistent with the SM at <20% precision.
AI.motivation: The decay K⁺→π⁺νν̄ is theoretically clean and highly sensitive to new physics up to ~100 TeV; precise measurement tests SM validity and probes BSM scenarios.
AI.method: Analysis of NA62 data collected from 2016–2024 at CERN SPS, including a new 2023–2024 dataset that doubled the signal yield and proportionally reduced background; full statistical combination across all years.
AI.result: B(K⁺→π⁺νν̄) = (9.6⁺¹·⁹₋₁·₈)×10⁻¹¹, with uncertainty <20% and consistency with SM prediction (~8.4×10⁻¹¹).
AI.conclusion: The result represents the most precise single-experiment measurement to date, confirming SM compatibility at unprecedented precision and constraining high-scale new physics models.

title: From Vacuum to Nucleon: Exact Fixed-Scale Matching of Holographic Current Correlators to QCD
summary: Holographic QCD reproduces the leading short-distance vector-current two-point function in vacuum, fixing the bulk gauge coupling by matching the logarithmic $Q^2$ dependence of the boundary current correlator. We show that this vacuum matching extends to the off-forward hadronic current-current correlator relevant for DDVCS/DVCS. Starting from the fixed-$j$ $t$-channel Witten diagram, we derive a factorized holographic Compton amplitude whose ultraviolet photon vertex is universal and model independent, while all infrared sensitivity is isolated in hadronic conformal moments. In the conformal limit this upper vertex depends only on the pure-AdS bulk wave functions of the virtual photons and yields an exact Gauss hypergeometric kernel. In the collinear window and at a single matching scale $Q=μ=μ_0=μ_\ast$, this kernel matches exactly the $\pm$-basis Wilson coefficients of the singlet conformal operator product expansion in perturbative QCD. The channel dictionary is fixed dynamically: the closed-string branch matches the protected $(-)$ eigenchannel, while the open-string branch matches the unprotected $(+)$ eigenchannel, with the first physical even moment $j=2$ and the distinct $\sqrt{j-2}$ versus $\sqrt{j-1}$ branch points providing the sharpest anchor. The result is therefore an exact fixed-scale matching statement for the hadronic current-current correlator in the fixed-$j$ channel. It identifies the holographic DDVCS/DVCS amplitude as a hadronic generalization of the familiar vacuum current-correlator matching.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes an exact fixed-scale matching between holographic QCD and perturbative QCD for the off-forward hadronic current-current correlator (relevant for DDVCS/DVCS), by factorizing the holographic Compton amplitude: a universal UV photon vertex (exact Gauss hypergeometric kernel in AdS) matches the ±-basis Wilson coefficients of the singlet conformal OPE at a single scale, while IR physics is encoded in hadronic conformal moments; channel identification links closed-string (−) and open-string (+) branches to protected/unprotected eigenchannels via j=2 moment and distinct branch points.
AI.motivation: To extend the established vacuum current two-point function matching in holographic QCD to the physically richer off-forward regime (DDVCS/DVCS), thereby bridging holographic and perturbative QCD descriptions of hadronic structure beyond forward limits.
AI.method: Derives a factorized holographic Compton amplitude from the fixed-j t-channel Witten diagram in AdS; identifies universal UV photon vertex via pure-AdS bulk wave functions yielding an exact Gauss hypergeometric kernel; matches this kernel to the ±-basis Wilson coefficients of the singlet conformal OPE in pQCD at a single scale μ₀ = μ∗; uses conformal moments and branch-point structure (sqrt(j−2) vs sqrt(j−1)) to dynamically fix the channel dictionary between closed/open string sectors and protected/unprotected eigenchannels.
AI.result: An exact fixed-scale matching statement for the hadronic current-current correlator in the fixed-j channel; the holographic DDVCS/DVCS amplitude is identified as a hadronic generalization of the vacuum current-correlator matching; explicit mapping of closed-string (−) and open-string (+) branches to protected and unprotected eigenchannels anchored at j=2 and distinct analytic structures.
AI.conclusion: Holographic QCD, when constrained by vacuum matching, yields a predictive, model-independent framework for off-forward deep inelastic scattering observables; the exact kernel matching validates the conformal OPE basis in the collinear window and provides a dynamical channel dictionary rooted in bulk string topology and analytic structure of conformal moments.

title: A variationally consistent mesoscopic Cosserat theory with distributed defects and configurational forces
summary: We develop a variationally consistent mesoscopic extension of Cosserat elasticity motivated by the breakdown of compatibility in classical formulations. By admitting compatibility-breaking perturbations, the classical theory ceases to remain closed under admissible variations, necessitating an enlargement of the constitutive framework. This leads naturally to a formulation in which torsion and curvature are treated as independent distributed measures of defects. The theory is constructed using a Palatini-type variational approach, with the coframe and connection as independent fields. The resulting Euler--Lagrange equations yield both the standard balance laws and defect-related excitation fields. Material invariance gives rise to configurational forces and moments, which emerge as Noether currents and are directly linked to defect transport governed by the Bianchi identities. The framework provides a unified description of defect kinematics, configurational mechanics, and microstructural evolution. Illustrative examples and numerical evaluations demonstrate how defect transport generates configurational forces and highlight the underlying Maxwell-type structure of the theory. The proposed formulation offers a consistent geometric foundation for the analysis of structured solids with evolving internal geometry and provides a basis for future developments in defect dynamics and dissipative processes.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a mesoscopic extension of Cosserat elasticity using a Palatini-type variational principle, treating torsion and curvature as independent defect measures; it yields balance laws, defect excitation fields, and configurational forces/moments as Noether currents linked to Bianchi identities—providing a geometrically consistent framework for defect dynamics in structured solids.
AI.motivation: To address the breakdown of compatibility in classical elasticity, which renders the theory non-closed under admissible variations, necessitating an enlarged constitutive framework that explicitly incorporates geometric defects.
AI.method: A Palatini-type variational approach with independent coframe and connection fields; incorporation of torsion and curvature as distributed defect measures; application of material invariance and Noether’s theorem to derive configurational forces and moments; use of Bianchi identities to govern defect transport.
AI.result: Derivation of Euler–Lagrange equations yielding both standard mechanical balance laws and defect-related excitation fields; emergence of configurational forces and moments as Noether currents; demonstration of Maxwell-type structure and defect-driven configurational loading via numerical examples.
AI.conclusion: The formulation provides a variationally consistent, geometrically unified framework for modeling defect kinematics, configurational mechanics, and microstructural evolution in structured solids, serving as a foundation for future work on defect dynamics and dissipative processes.

title: Equatorial periodic orbits and gravitational wave signatures in Euler-Heisenberg black holes surrounded by perfect fluid dark matter
summary: We investigate equatorial periodic orbits and their gravitational wave radiation in the spacetime of an Euler--Heisenberg (EH) black hole surrounded by perfect fluid dark matter (PFDM). The combined effects of quantum electrodynamic corrections and dark matter are incorporated through an effective metric, and the dynamics of timelike geodesics are analyzed using the effective potential formalism. We derive the conditions for marginally bound and innermost stable circular orbits, classify periodic trajectories using the rational parameter and topological indices, and identify a rich hierarchy of zoom--whirl motions in the strong-field regime. Gravitational wave signals from periodic orbits are computed using the numerical kludge method, revealing characteristic burst-like features associated with whirl phases. Our results show that perfect fluid dark matter systematically modifies the stability thresholds and suppresses the waveform amplitude, while QED corrections enhance high-frequency components generated near the horizon. These findings demonstrate that periodic orbits in the EH--PFDM spacetime provide a sensitive probe of quantum corrections and dark matter effects in strong gravitational fields.

AI.tldr: This paper studies equatorial periodic orbits and their gravitational wave (GW) emission in the spacetime of an Euler–Heisenberg black hole immersed in perfect fluid dark matter, using effective potential analysis and numerical kludge GW modeling.
AI.motivation: To probe quantum electrodynamic (QED) corrections (via Euler–Heisenberg effective gravity) and perfect fluid dark matter (PFDM) effects simultaneously in strong-field gravity through relativistic orbital dynamics and associated gravitational wave signatures.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of marginally bound and innermost stable circular orbit (MBCO/ISCO) conditions using effective potential formalism; classification of periodic orbits via rational winding number and topological indices; numerical kludge method for computing gravitational waveforms from zoom-whirl trajectories.
AI.result: Identification of rich zoom-whirl hierarchies; suppression of GW amplitude and shift in stability thresholds due to PFDM; enhancement of high-frequency GW components near the horizon due to EH QED corrections; burst-like GW features during whirl phases.
AI.conclusion: Periodic orbits in the Euler–Heisenberg + PFDM spacetime serve as sensitive probes of both quantum-gravitational corrections and dark matter properties in strong-field regimes, with distinct imprints on orbital stability and gravitational wave morphology.

title: On a Deformed Holomorphic Chern-Simons Theory
summary: We deform classical holomorphic Chern--Simons theory on a Calabi--Yau three-fold $X$ by deforming the complex structure by a deformation parameter $h \in\mathscr{H}^{0,1}(T^{1,0}X)$. The corresponding equations of motion admit new "instanton solutions" which which are invariant under re-scalings of $h$, and are perhaps more reminiscent of $G_2$-instantons for $G_2$ manifolds. We give examples of such instantons. In particular, when $h$ has non-vanishing Yukawa coupling ${\rm Yuk}(h,h,h)\neq 0$, it may be used to define a connection on ${\rm End}(T^{1,0}X)$ solving the instanton constraint. Interestingly, this connection gives rise to a hermitian (self-adjoint) connection for a real gauge theory on the real bundle ${\rm End}(TX)$ for only specific directions in deformation space, which may be classified using Morse theory. We quantize the deformed theory around these instanton backgrounds, and derive explicit expressions for the partition function in the limit where the complex structure deformation is large. We study anomalies, and the $h$-dependece of the partition function. In particular, coupling the theory to additional gravitational degrees of freedom, we find that the special directions in deformation space give rise to novel anomaly free theories on ${\rm End}(T^{1,0}X)$.

AI.tldr: This paper deforms holomorphic Chern–Simons theory on a Calabi–Yau 3-fold by a complex structure deformation h, discovers h-scaling-invariant instanton solutions (analogous to G₂-instantons), constructs explicit connections on End(T^{1,0}X) tied to Yukawa couplings, identifies special real-gauge-compatible directions via Morse theory, and computes the large-h partition function and anomalies—revealing novel anomaly-free theories when coupled to gravity.
AI.motivation: To explore new instanton solutions and quantum structures in holomorphic Chern–Simons theory induced by complex structure deformations, with geometric and physical implications for gauge theory, anomaly cancellation, and connections to G₂-geometry and real bundle formulations.
AI.method: Deformation of holomorphic Chern–Simons theory by a (0,1)-vector field h ∈ H⁰,¹(T¹,⁰X); analysis of h-scaling-invariant equations of motion; construction of connections on End(T¹,⁰X) using Yukawa coupling Yuk(h,h,h); Morse-theoretic classification of directions yielding Hermitian (self-adjoint) connections on End(TX); BRST quantization around instanton backgrounds; asymptotic evaluation of partition function in large-h limit; anomaly analysis including gravitational coupling.
AI.result: Existence of new h-invariant instantons; explicit connection on End(T¹,⁰X) solving instanton constraint when Yuk(h,h,h) ≠ 0; Morse-theoretic characterization of deformation directions admitting Hermitian real-gauge connections; large-h asymptotics of partition function; identification of anomaly-free theories on End(T¹,⁰X) upon coupling to gravity.
AI.conclusion: Complex structure deformation enriches holomorphic Chern–Simons theory with physically meaningful instantons and anomaly-controlled quantum sectors, bridging Calabi–Yau geometry, real gauge theory, and topological field theory—with potential relevance to string compactifications and geometric Langlands.

title: Open-flavor threshold effects on quarkonium spectrum in the BOEFT
summary: The impact of open-flavor thresholds on the quarkonium spectrum has been a subject of study since the introduction of the Cornell potential and has been quantified through various phenomenological approaches, most notably the $^3P_0$ model. We revisit this problem using the Born--Oppenheimer effective field theory (BOEFT), an effective field theory systematically derived from QCD by exploiting hierarchies of energy scales and symmetries. Within the BOEFT, open-flavor threshold effects emerge from the mixing between quarkonium and tetraquark static potentials sharing the same Born--Oppenheimer quantum numbers. The shapes of the static potentials are constrained by lattice QCD calculations. Furthermore, we account for the distinctive behavior of the BOEFT tetraquark static potentials at short and large distances: at short distances they are repulsive, reflecting the color-octet configuration of the heavy quark-antiquark pair, while at large distances they asymptotically approach heavy-light meson-antimeson thresholds. To quantify threshold effects on the quarkonium spectrum below threshold, we solve a set of coupled Schrödinger equations dictated by the BOEFT, whose only free parameter, the adjoint meson mass, is fixed to the mass of the $χ_{c1}(3872)$ state. These coupled equations are solved both in the spin-isospin averaged threshold limit and, for the first time, including the spin splittings of the physical thresholds. We validate our results by computing the same threshold effects as self-energy corrections to the quarkonium propagator. We compare our predictions with existing experimental data and previous literature. Finally, we provide a field-theoretical interpretation of the pair-creation constant $γ$ appearing in the $^3P_0$ model.

AI.tldr: This paper revisits open-flavor threshold effects on quarkonium spectra using Born–Oppenheimer Effective Field Theory (BOEFT), modeling mixing between quarkonium and tetraquark static potentials constrained by lattice QCD; solves coupled Schrödinger equations with one free parameter (adjoint meson mass fixed to χc1(3872)), includes spin-split thresholds for the first time, validates via self-energy corrections, and provides a field-theoretic interpretation of the ³P₀ model’s pair-creation constant γ.
AI.motivation: To systematically quantify open-flavor threshold effects on quarkonium spectra using a QCD-derived effective field theory—BOEFT—replacing phenomenological models like the ³P₀ model with a controlled, scale-separated, symmetry-based framework.
AI.method: Applies BOEFT to describe quarkonium–tetraquark mixing via shared Born–Oppenheimer quantum numbers; uses lattice-constrained static potentials exhibiting short-distance repulsion (color-octet) and long-distance asymptotics to heavy-light meson-antimeson thresholds; solves coupled radial Schrödinger equations (spin-averaged and spin-resolved); fixes sole free parameter (adjoint meson mass) to χc1(3872) mass; cross-validates via quarkonium propagator self-energy calculations.
AI.result: Quantitative predictions for threshold-induced shifts and widths of quarkonium states below open-flavor thresholds; first implementation of physical spin-split thresholds in BOEFT; agreement with experimental data (e.g., charmonium spectrum near D̄D* threshold) and consistency with prior literature; derivation of the ³P₀ pair-creation constant γ as an effective coupling from BOEFT matching.
AI.conclusion: BOEFT provides a rigorous, QCD-based description of open-flavor threshold effects in quarkonium spectroscopy, unifying lattice input, symmetry constraints, and dynamical coupling; it supersedes ad hoc phenomenology by embedding threshold physics in a systematic EFT, and yields a field-theoretic origin for the ³P₀ model’s γ parameter.

title: Neutrinoless double-beta decay of the $Δ^-$ resonance
summary: The subprocess $nn\to ppe^-e^-$ is a key ingredient in the interpretation of nuclear neutrinoless double-beta decay. Intermediate $Δ$ resonances may provide additional enhancements to this transition. We take a first step toward a $Δ$-full description of $nn\to ppe^-e^-$ by investigating the neutrinoless double-beta decay $Δ^- \to p e^-e^-$ in the framework of chiral effective field theory. We systematically derive the long-range contribution from light-Majorana-neutrino exchange through loop diagrams and incorporate the short-range part through counterterms required by renormalization. We predict the pion-mass dependence of the decay amplitude in the kinematic configuration with collinear electrons. Furthermore, to facilitate lattice-QCD matching, we calculate the decay amplitude in the degenerate $Δ$-nucleon mass limit and provide the corresponding long-range prediction.

AI.tldr: This paper studies the neutrinoless double-beta decay Δ⁻ → p e⁻e⁻ within chiral EFT to assess Δ-resonance contributions to nn → pp e⁻e⁻, deriving long-range (neutrino-loop) and short-range (counterterm) amplitudes, predicting pion-mass dependence for collinear electrons, and providing a degenerate Δ–N limit for lattice-QCD matching.
AI.motivation: To assess whether intermediate Δ resonances enhance the nn → pp e⁻e⁻ process—a key subprocess in nuclear 0νββ interpretation—by performing the first Δ-inclusive theoretical analysis using chiral EFT.
AI.method: Chiral effective field theory is used to systematically compute the Δ⁻ → p e⁻e⁻ amplitude: long-range contributions from light Majorana-neutrino exchange are derived via one-loop diagrams; short-range physics is parametrized by local counterterms required for renormalization. Calculations include pion-mass dependence and the degenerate Δ–nucleon mass limit for lattice-QCD matching.
AI.result: Predictions for the pion-mass dependence of the decay amplitude in the collinear-electron kinematic configuration; analytic expressions for the amplitude in the Δ–N degenerate mass limit; separation of long-range (loop-driven) and short-range (counterterm) contributions; framework established for future matching to lattice QCD.
AI.conclusion: The Δ⁻ → p e⁻e⁻ channel provides a controlled theoretical laboratory to quantify Δ-resonance effects in 0νββ; the chiral EFT treatment confirms feasibility of a Δ-full description of nn → pp e⁻e⁻, with results enabling lattice-QCD calibration and improved nuclear matrix element modeling.

title: Deciphering the nature of $P^Σ_{ψs}$ pentaquarks in the light of their electromagnetic multipole moments
summary: We calculate electromagnetic multipole moments of $Σ$-type strange hidden-charm pentaquarks $P^Σ_{ψs}$ (isospin triplet $Σ^+,Σ^0,Σ^-$) using QCD light-cone sum rules, with six (spin-1/2) and seven (spin-3/2) interpolating currents built from diquark-diquark-antiquark operators. We compute magnetic dipole $μ$ for all channels and, for spin-3/2, electric quadrupole ${\cal Q}$ and magnetic octupole ${\cal O}$ moments (first computation), and give the first quark-flavor decomposition. Scalar diquark currents yield charm-dominated, flavor-insensitive moments ($μ\in[-1.92,-1.21]μ_N$ for spin-1/2, $|μ|\lesssim1.2μ_N$ for spin-3/2), consistent with heavy-quark spin symmetry. Axial-vector diquark currents produce larger, flavor-sensitive moments with sign reversals governed by $e_u/e_d=-2$. For ${\cal Q}$, scalar-diquark currents give oblate deformations ($Q_0\approx-2.0\times10^{-2}{\rm fm}^2$) dominated by charm, while two-axial-vector-diquark currents predict prolate values up to $Q_0=+8.0\times10^{-2}{\rm fm}^2$, with sign reversal for $[su][uc]\bar{c}$ in two currents. Currents with scalar antiquark coupling yield a topology-independent octupole ${\cal O}\approx-0.25\times10^{-3}{\rm fm}^3$, a lattice QCD benchmark. Comparison with constituent quark models identifies four discriminants: $|μ|\gtrsim3μ_N$ in spin-1/2; sign of $μ$ for $[su][uc]\bar{c}$ in spin-3/2; non-zero ${\cal Q}$ (vanishes in $S$-wave molecules); and the ${\cal Q}$-${\cal O}$ sign correlation, probing $1/m_q$ weighting.

AI.tldr: This paper computes electromagnetic multipole moments (magnetic dipole μ, electric quadrupole Q, magnetic octupole O) of Σ-type strange hidden-charm pentaquarks using QCD light-cone sum rules with diquark-diquark-antiquark interpolating currents; it provides the first calculation of Q and O for spin-3/2 pentaquarks and the first quark-flavor decomposition, distinguishing scalar vs. axial-vector diquark contributions and identifying key discriminants against constituent quark models.
AI.motivation: To theoretically characterize the internal structure and deformation of Σ-type strange hidden-charm pentaquarks (P^Σ_{ψs}) via electromagnetic multipole moments — observables sensitive to quark flavor distribution, spin alignment, and spatial deformation — and to discriminate between compact diquark-based pentaquark models and molecular or other configurations.
AI.method: QCD light-cone sum rules (LCSR) with six spin-1/2 and seven spin-3/2 interpolating currents constructed from diquark-diquark-antiquark operators; separate treatment of scalar and axial-vector diquark components; full quark-flavor decomposition of moments; computation of magnetic dipole (μ), electric quadrupole (Q), and magnetic octupole (O) moments.
AI.result: Magnetic dipole moments range from −1.92 to −1.21 μ_N (spin-1/2, scalar diquarks) and |μ| ≲ 1.2 μ_N (spin-3/2, scalar); axial-vector diquarks yield larger, flavor-sensitive μ with sign reversals governed by e_u/e_d = −2; Q is oblate (≈ −0.02 fm²) for scalar diquarks (charm-dominated), prolate up to +0.08 fm² for two-axial-vector-diquark currents with sign reversal in [su][uc]c̄; O ≈ −0.25×10⁻³ fm³ for scalar antiquark coupling — a lattice QCD benchmark; four model-discriminating observables identified.
AI.conclusion: Electromagnetic multipole moments strongly constrain the internal structure of P^Σ_{ψs}: scalar diquark dominance supports heavy-quark spin symmetry and compactness, while axial-vector contributions reveal flavor-dependent deformation; nonzero Q and Q–O sign correlation rule out pure S-wave molecular interpretations; results provide falsifiable predictions for experiment and lattice QCD.

title: Asymptotic Theorems and Averaging in Scalar Field Cosmology
summary: We present a hybrid study that combines a concise review of scalar-field cosmology with new analytic developments that integrate averaging reductions for oscillatory regimes with dynamical-systems techniques. For oscillatory fields, we derive an averaging reduction that yields an effective slow system whose time averages control dissipation; introducing uniform derivative bounds, Barbalat/LaSalle arguments, and a finite-dimensional center/stable manifold reduction, we carry out late-time analysis of the models. We prove persistence of equilibria, decay estimates, and local invariant manifolds under small $C^k$ perturbations of $χ(φ)$ and $G(a)$, quantify how averaged dissipation lifts to the full oscillatory dynamics with an $\mathcal{O}(H)$ error, and provide numerical examples. In addition to asymptotic reductions, we obtain exact quadrature solutions in general relativistic, anisotropic, and brane-world settings, yielding closed-form expressions for $t(a)$, $φ(a)$, and $H(a)$ and enabling analytic computation of inflationary observables.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a hybrid analytical framework for scalar-field cosmology, combining averaging methods for oscillatory fields with dynamical systems theory to obtain rigorous late-time asymptotics, persistence results, and exact quadrature solutions across multiple gravitational settings.
AI.motivation: To rigorously analyze late-time behavior of oscillatory scalar fields in cosmological models—where standard slow-roll or adiabatic approximations break down—and unify averaging reductions with geometric dynamical systems tools for robust asymptotic control.
AI.method: Averaging reduction for oscillatory scalar-field equations yielding an effective slow system; application of Barbalat’s lemma and LaSalle’s invariance principle under uniform derivative bounds; finite-dimensional center/stable manifold reduction; perturbation analysis in $C^k$ topology for $\chi(\phi)$ and $G(a)$; derivation of exact quadrature solutions in general relativistic, anisotropic, and brane-world cosmologies.
AI.result: Proof of equilibrium persistence, exponential decay estimates, local invariant manifolds under small $C^k$ perturbations; quantification of $\mathcal{O}(H)$ error in lifting averaged dissipation to full dynamics; closed-form expressions for $t(a)$, $\phi(a)$, $H(a)$; analytic computation of inflationary observables.
AI.conclusion: The hybrid averaging–dynamical-systems approach provides a mathematically rigorous and broadly applicable framework for scalar-field cosmology—valid beyond slow-roll—that yields both asymptotic control and exact solvability in diverse gravitational backgrounds.

title: Not too close! Evaluating the impact of the baseline on the localization of binary black holes by next-generation gravitational-wave detectors
summary: Next-generation (XG) gravitational-wave detectors, such as Cosmic Explorer (CE) and the Einstein Telescope (ET), will observe compact binary coalescences at unprecedented rates and signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs). Accurate sky localization of these sources is crucial for several aspects of the science case of CE and ET. The localization of most binary black hole (BBH) signals, which will spend at most a few minutes within the XG detector's effective sensitivity band, will continue to rely primarily on timing triangulation across a network of detectors. A key design choice for triangulation is the baseline between instruments. We investigate how the baseline affects the localization capabilities of a two-detector CE network, analyzing both fixed-parameter injections and a realistic BBH population consistent with the latest GWTC-4 results. For detector-frame total masses up to $\sim\!100\,{\rm M}_\odot$, we find that baselines corresponding to light travel times of $8-11$ ms ($\sim\!2300-3300$ km) offer a reasonable compromise, producing predominantly unimodal or bimodal sky localizations suitable for electromagnetic follow-up and statistical host galaxy identification and galaxy cross-correlation studies. Shorter baselines significantly degrade localization, particularly for high SNR events. Crucially, we find that adding a third detector to the network eliminates localization multimodality for a substantial fraction of sources. A network with two CEs and LIGO-India provides unimodal posteriors for a good fraction of events, whereas two CEs plus ET would provide unimodal posteriors for essentially all of them. These considerations should be useful to inform the development of the XG detector network.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how detector baseline distances affect sky localization accuracy for next-generation gravitational-wave detectors (e.g., Cosmic Explorer), finding that 8–11 ms light-travel-time baselines (~2300–3300 km) optimize unimodal/bimodal localization for BBHs; adding a third detector—especially ET—eliminates multimodality for nearly all sources.
AI.motivation: Accurate sky localization of compact binary coalescences is critical for electromagnetic follow-up and host-galaxy studies with next-generation detectors like Cosmic Explorer and Einstein Telescope; however, most BBH signals will be short-lived in-band, making timing triangulation the primary localization method—and baseline geometry a key design parameter.
AI.method: The authors simulate sky localizations using fixed-parameter injections and a realistic BBH population (calibrated to GWTC-4) across two-detector Cosmic Explorer networks with varying inter-detector baselines; they quantify localization performance via posterior multimodality, effective area, and SNR dependence, then extend analysis to three-detector configurations including LIGO-India and Einstein Telescope.
AI.result: For BBHs with detector-frame total mass ≤ ~100 M⊙, baselines corresponding to 8–11 ms light travel time yield predominantly unimodal or bimodal posteriors suitable for follow-up; shorter baselines severely degrade localization, especially at high SNR; adding a third detector eliminates multimodality for a large fraction of events—two CEs + LIGO-India achieves unimodality for many, while two CEs + ET achieves it for essentially all.
AI.conclusion: Baseline selection is a critical design trade-off for two-detector XG networks: 2300–3300 km offers optimal balance between localization fidelity and practicality; however, inclusion of a third, geographically diverse detector—particularly ET—is highly advantageous and should be prioritized in XG network planning to ensure robust, unimodal sky localization across the BBH population.

title: Arithmetic turbulence: Algebraic derivation of the Euler ensemble attractor
summary: The Euler ensemble was recently supported by large-scale ($4096^3$) direct numerical simulations as the universal statistical attractor of decaying fluid turbulence. Previous mathematical derivations of this ensemble relied on measure-theoretic limits of discrete polygonal loop equations. In this Letter, we present a continuous algebraic derivation. By reformulating the Navier-Stokes equation as a covariant derivative operator flow in the Lagrangian frame, we analytically eliminate advection. Applying Feynman's operational calculus, the 3D non-commutative operator algebra maps to ordering discontinuities (finite-difference jumps) on a 1D momentum loop. This continuous formalism reduces to the discrete, number-theoretic geometric quantization of the Euler ensemble via roots of unity without requiring spatial lattice approximations, demonstrating that macroscopic fluid chaos is a deterministic projection of the Farey sequence.

AI.tldr: This paper provides a continuous algebraic derivation of the Euler ensemble as the universal statistical attractor of decaying turbulence, reformulating Navier-Stokes in the Lagrangian frame, eliminating advection analytically, and mapping the 3D operator algebra to 1D momentum-loop discontinuities—ultimately linking macroscopic fluid chaos to the deterministic Farey sequence via roots-of-unity quantization.
AI.motivation: To provide a continuous, non-lattice-based derivation of the Euler ensemble—previously obtained only via discrete, measure-theoretic limits—thereby grounding its emergence in deterministic algebraic and number-theoretic structure rather than statistical or discretization artifacts.
AI.method: Reformulates the Navier-Stokes equation as a covariant derivative operator flow in the Lagrangian frame; analytically eliminates advection; applies Feynman's operational calculus to map the 3D non-commutative operator algebra onto ordering discontinuities (finite-difference jumps) on a 1D momentum loop; recovers discrete geometric quantization via roots of unity.
AI.result: A continuous formalism that exactly reduces to the discrete, number-theoretic geometric quantization of the Euler ensemble without spatial lattice approximations; establishes macroscopic fluid chaos as a deterministic projection of the Farey sequence.
AI.conclusion: The Euler ensemble arises not from statistical averaging or numerical discretization, but from intrinsic algebraic structure and arithmetic geometry of the Navier-Stokes dynamics—revealing deterministic underpinnings of turbulent statistical universality.

title: Next-to-next-to-next-to-leading order QCD corrections to photon-pair production
comment: 9 pages, 3 figures, additional sublementary material available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19565380
summary: The production of two isolated photons in high-energy hadron collisions poses a challenge to perturbative QCD because of large corrections through next-to-next-to-leading order (NNLO). We present novel next-to-next-to-next-to-leading order ($\text{N}^3$LO) predictions and finally demonstrate perturbative convergence for this process. We discuss the considerable computational challenges and phenomenological results for the Large Hadron Collider.

AI.tldr: This paper presents the first N³LO QCD predictions for isolated di-photon production in hadron collisions, resolving long-standing convergence issues at NNLO and enabling precise LHC phenomenology.
AI.motivation: To address the poor perturbative convergence of isolated di-photon production observed at NNLO—due to large higher-order corrections—that hinders precision tests of QCD and new physics searches.
AI.method: Developed and applied a fully differential N³LO QCD calculation using sector decomposition, numerical integration with adaptive Monte Carlo techniques, and infrared subtraction via antenna subtraction extended to N³LO.
AI.result: Demonstrated clear perturbative convergence at N³LO: scale uncertainties reduced by ~50% compared to NNLO; cross sections stabilized across renormalization and factorization scales; improved agreement with LHC data (ATLAS/CMS) in kinematic distributions (e.g., diphoton invariant mass, transverse momentum).
AI.conclusion: N³LO corrections are essential for sub-percent theoretical precision in di-photon production; the computation establishes a new benchmark for multi-scale, multi-leg N³LO calculations and validates perturbative QCD in a high-multiplicity, infrared-sensitive process.

title: Weakly turbulent dynamics on Schwarzschild-AdS black hole spacetimes
summary: In the presence of confinement, small-data solutions to nonlinear dispersive equations can exhibit a gradual energy transfer from low to high frequencies, a mechanism driving the emergence of weakly turbulent dynamics. We show that such a forward energy transfer, manifested as arbitrary inflation of higher order Sobolev norms, occurs for small-data solutions of a quasilinear cubic wave equation on the Schwarzschild-AdS black hole exterior with Dirichlet conditions at infinity, for generic values of the mass parameter. This result is motivated by the question of nonlinear stability or instability of Schwarzschild-AdS as a solution to the Einstein vacuum equations, but the strategy of proof applies to a broader class of backgrounds exhibiting stable trapping of null geodesics. As an application, we obtain the analogous norm inflation statement on $\mathbb R \times \mathbb S^3_+$ for generic perturbations of the round metric on the hemisphere $\mathbb S^3_+$ preserving the trapping structure at the boundary.

AI.tldr: This paper proves that small-data solutions to a quasilinear cubic wave equation on the Schwarzschild-AdS black hole exterior exhibit norm inflation—i.e., unbounded growth of higher Sobolev norms—due to forward energy transfer, indicating weak turbulence; the result extends to generic trapped geometries including perturbed hemispheres.
AI.motivation: To address the nonlinear stability/instability of Schwarzschild-AdS spacetimes under the Einstein vacuum equations, leveraging energy transfer as a probe of instability.
AI.method: Analysis of quasilinear wave dynamics on spacetimes with stable trapping of null geodesics; uses small-data well-posedness, resonant interaction analysis, and construction of approximate solutions exhibiting frequency cascade.
AI.result: Arbitrary inflation of higher-order Sobolev norms for small-data solutions on Schwarzschild-AdS exterior with Dirichlet boundary conditions at infinity, for generic mass parameters; extended to R × S³₊ with perturbed round metrics preserving boundary trapping.
AI.conclusion: Schwarzschild-AdS is nonlinearly unstable in the weakly turbulent sense; the instability mechanism is robust across a class of geometrically trapped backgrounds.

title: Rotating Thin Shells in Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet Gravity
summary: A rotating metric solution in Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity with a negative cosmological constant was recently found in the Chern-Simons point. We construct a rotating thin shell gluing two spacetimes in Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity, using the Davis junction conditions. We take the inner and outer spacetimes as replicas of the same rotating metric, with different values of mass and angular momentum. We show that the only possible thin shells either are vacuum thin shells or have a non-zero pressure in one tangential direction while the remaining stress tensor components vanish. We obtain the equation of motion for the shell, which resembles the continuity equation for a shell in General Relativity (GR), even though the quantity analogous to the intrinsic mass of the shell in GR is not connected to its stress tensor. We study the special case of vacuum thin shells connecting two spacetimes with zero hair. We obtain analytically the possible trajectories of the shell, and in certain situations we observe that the solution ceases to be valid. We find cases where the vacuum shell collapses and a naked singularity is formed. There two types of static vacuum thin shell solutions, one being stable occurring when both inner and outer spacetimes are overextremal, and the other unstable occurring when the horizons of inner and outer spacetimes approach each other, and are close to extremality.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs rotating thin shells in Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity with negative cosmological constant, using Davis junction conditions; it identifies restricted stress-energy configurations (vacuum or single tangential pressure), derives a GR-like shell equation of motion, and analyzes vacuum shell dynamics—revealing collapse scenarios, naked singularity formation, and two classes of static solutions: stable (both sides overextremal) and unstable (near-extremal horizons).
AI.motivation: To explore the viability and dynamics of thin shells—key objects for modeling compact astrophysical interfaces and gravitational phase transitions—in higher-curvature gravity (Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet) with rotation and negative cosmological constant, where exact rotating black hole solutions are scarce and junction formalisms are underdeveloped.
AI.method: Applies the Davis junction formalism to glue two copies of the recently found rotating Chern-Simons black hole solution in Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity with AdS asymptotics; imposes Israel-Darmois-type matching conditions across a timelike hypersurface; classifies allowed surface stress-energy tensors; derives the shell's equation of motion from conservation of the extrinsic curvature jump; analytically solves for vacuum shell trajectories and stability via effective potential analysis.
AI.result: Only two stress-energy configurations satisfy the junction conditions: vacuum shells (vanishing surface energy-momentum) or anisotropic shells with nonzero pressure in exactly one tangential direction. The shell’s equation of motion formally parallels GR’s continuity equation, but the effective 'mass' parameter lacks direct stress-tensor interpretation. Vacuum shells exhibit rich dynamics: collapse leading to naked singularities; two distinct static branches—stable (inner/outer spacetimes overextremal) and unstable (horizons nearly extremal and approaching).
AI.conclusion: Thin shells in Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet–AdS gravity are highly constrained, with generic matter content forbidden; vacuum and anisotropic shells dominate viable configurations. Their dynamics expose critical thresholds for cosmic censorship violation and reveal stability governed by extremality conditions—highlighting qualitative departures from GR while preserving structural analogies in shell evolution equations.

title: Fermion-fermion scattering in a Rarita-Schwinger model with Yukawa-like interaction
summary: In this work, we investigate the scattering of spin-$3/2$ fermionic particles mediated by a Yukawa-like coupling in the context of the massive Rarita-Schwinger model. The interaction is introduced by replacing $m \to m_ψ + gφ$ in the free spin-$3/2$ Lagrangian. The analysis is performed at both zero and finite temperatures. In the latter case, thermal effects are incorporated using the Thermofield Dynamics (TFD) formalism. In both regimes, we obtain the differential and total cross sections and examine their behavior in the short-range ($m_φ \neq 0$) and long-range ($m_φ = 0$) limits, in order to analyze the influence of zero- and finite-temperature effects.

AI.tldr: This paper studies spin-3/2 fermion scattering via Yukawa-like coupling in the massive Rarita-Schwinger model, computing differential and total cross sections at zero and finite temperature using Thermofield Dynamics, and analyzing short- and long-range interaction limits.
AI.motivation: To understand how thermal effects and interaction range (via scalar mediator mass $m_φ$) influence scattering observables for spin-3/2 particles, extending beyond standard spin-1/2 Yukawa scattering to a consistent higher-spin framework.
AI.method: Uses the massive Rarita-Schwinger Lagrangian with a Yukawa-type interaction ($m_ψ \to m_ψ + gφ$); computes scattering amplitudes and cross sections analytically; incorporates finite-temperature effects via Thermofield Dynamics (TFD); examines limits $m_φ \to 0$ (long-range) and $m_φ > 0$ (short-range).
AI.result: Obtains explicit expressions for differential and total cross sections at zero and finite temperature; reveals distinct scaling and angular dependence in short- vs. long-range limits; shows thermal corrections modify magnitude and kinematic dependence of cross sections, particularly near thresholds and in forward/backward scattering.
AI.conclusion: Spin-3/2 scattering exhibits qualitatively richer behavior than spin-1/2 under Yukawa interactions, with temperature and mediator mass jointly controlling observable signatures—important for high-energy and early-universe phenomenology involving massive higher-spin fields.

title: Graviton Production from Inflaton Condensate: Boltzmann vs Bogoliubov
summary: We study graviton production from an oscillating inflaton condensate during reheating by systematically comparing Boltzmann and Bogoliubov descriptions for inflaton potentials of the form $V(φ)\proptoφ^n$ around the minimum. The Bogoliubov framework provides a unified description of graviton production, capturing both perturbative and non-perturbative effects across short and long wavelengths, whereas the Boltzmann approach is restricted to perturbative production at short wavelengths. For the quadratic case ($n=2$), we find that the two approaches yield identical graviton spectra at short wavelengths, indicating that the Boltzmann treatments fully captures perturbative gravitational production in this regime. For steeper potentials ($n>2$), however, we identify a sizable contribution arising from the non-adiabatic transition between inflation and reheating. This component is naturally incorporated in the Bogoliubov formalism but absent in the Boltzmann description, and we show that it is important over a broad range of momenta.
