We derive analytic approximations within both frameworks that clarify the physical origin and scaling behavior of the spectrum. Our results delineate the regime of validity of Boltzmann approaches and show that, for steeper inflaton potentials, graviton production is governed by non-adiabatic transition dynamics for which the Bogoliubov formalism provides the most appropriate description.

AI.tldr: This paper compares Boltzmann and Bogoliubov formalisms for graviton production during reheating after inflation, showing that the Bogoliubov method universally captures both perturbative (short-wavelength) and non-perturbative (long-wavelength, non-adiabatic transition) contributions, while the Boltzmann approach fails for steeper inflaton potentials (n > 2) due to its perturbative limitation.
AI.motivation: To determine the regime of validity of Boltzmann methods for graviton production during reheating and assess whether non-perturbative, non-adiabatic effects—especially at the inflation-reheating transition—are adequately captured by standard kinetic treatments.
AI.method: Systematic comparison of graviton production spectra computed via Boltzmann transport equations and Bogoliubov coefficient evolution, applied to monomial inflaton potentials V(φ) ∝ φ^n near the minimum; derivation of analytic approximations for spectral scaling in both frameworks.
AI.result: For n = 2 (quadratic potential), Boltzmann and Bogoliubov agree at short wavelengths; for n > 2, Bogoliubov reveals a significant non-adiabatic transition contribution absent in Boltzmann, dominant over a broad momentum range; analytic expressions confirm distinct scaling behaviors tied to adiabaticity violation.
AI.conclusion: Boltzmann approaches are insufficient for graviton production from steep inflaton potentials (n > 2); the Bogoliubov formalism is necessary to correctly describe non-adiabatic, non-perturbative graviton generation across all wavelengths.

title: Mass creation by the strong interaction: Glueballs -- status and perspectives
summary: Glueballs represent a fascinating aspect of the strong interaction in nature. Gluons that serve as the mediators of the strong interaction are massless particles, but they possess a property unique to the strong interaction called color charge, which is analogous to electric charge in the electromagnetic interaction. Glueballs are composed of multiple gluons and would be massless without color charges. The interaction of the color charges, however, makes glueballs becoming massive objects. Glueballs thus offer a unique way to study the mass creation of strongly interacting particles.

AI.tldr: This paper discusses glueballs—exotic hadrons composed solely of gluons—and emphasizes their role in understanding mass generation in quantum chromodynamics (QCD) via color-charge interactions.
AI.motivation: To explore how glueballs, as color-singlet bound states of gluons, provide insight into non-perturbative QCD and the dynamical origin of mass in strongly interacting systems.
AI.method: Conceptual/theoretical analysis based on QCD principles, focusing on gluon self-interactions and color confinement.
AI.result: Glueballs acquire mass through self-interactions mediated by color charge, despite constituent gluons being massless—a key manifestation of dynamical mass generation in QCD.
AI.conclusion: Glueballs serve as a critical probe of non-perturbative strong interaction dynamics and the mechanism by which mass emerges in the absence of elementary mass terms.

title: Relativistic signatures of scalar dark matter in extreme-mass-ratio inspirals
summary: We study gravitational wave emission by circular extreme-mass-ratio systems in a spherically symmetric scalar environment. Previous studies have focused on the impact of scalar radiation channels, revealing a rich structure of resonances, sharp features and floating orbits. Through the backreaction of the cloud on the metric, corrections to the gravitational sector come in at the same order. We develop the computational methods, and provide a characterization of this new, fully relativistic cloud signature. Remarkably, corrections to the polar sector can dominate all other dissipative corrections. We identify scalar field masses $Mμ\lesssim 0.12$ as the regime where polar can overtake axial and scalar channels at small separation. For small $Mμ$, vacuum dephasing is dominated mostly by conservative and polar cloud corrections, with scalar radiation acting as only a minor correction. At large $Mμ$, both terms terms are shown to be highly non-negligible. Our results therefore motivate including these relativistic signatures in beyond-vacuum EMRI templates.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates gravitational wave emission from extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) in a scalar-field environment, identifying dominant relativistic corrections—especially in the polar sector—from the backreaction of a scalar cloud on spacetime; it finds that polar dissipative effects can surpass axial and scalar radiation channels for certain scalar field masses, urging their inclusion in beyond-vacuum EMRI waveform templates.
AI.motivation: To characterize relativistic signatures from scalar-field environments in EMRIs—beyond prior focus on scalar radiation alone—and assess their impact on gravitational wave phasing for accurate template modeling.
AI.method: Develops fully relativistic computational methods to model the backreaction of a scalar cloud on the spacetime metric in spherically symmetric backgrounds, decomposing perturbations into polar and axial sectors and computing dissipative and conservative corrections to orbital evolution.
AI.result: Polar-sector corrections dominate dissipative effects over axial and scalar radiation channels for scalar mass parameter $M\mu \lesssim 0.12$ at small separations; for small $M\mu$, vacuum dephasing is driven mainly by conservative + polar cloud terms, while scalar radiation is subdominant; at large $M\mu$, both polar and scalar contributions remain highly significant.
AI.conclusion: Relativistic polar corrections from scalar cloud backreaction constitute a leading-order signature in EMRI waveforms and must be incorporated into beyond-vacuum template banks for precision tests of scalar-tensor gravity with LISA.

title: Symmetries of massless QCD
comment: 48 pages, 8 figures. arXiv admin note: substantial text overlap with arXiv:hep-ph/0010049
summary: We present a pedagogical review of certain exact theoretical results concerning the physics of an imaginary world where one quark or more are deprived of their masses.

AI.tldr: A pedagogical review of exact theoretical results in a hypothetical scenario where one or more quarks are massless.
AI.motivation: To provide an accessible, pedagogical exposition of exact theoretical results in chiral (massless-quark) limits of QCD-like theories.
AI.method: Theoretical analysis and synthesis of exact results—e.g., chiral symmetry breaking, anomalies, Ward identities, and topological effects—in the limit of vanishing quark masses.
AI.result: Clarification and systematization of non-perturbative consequences of chiral symmetry, including Goldstone bosons, the chiral anomaly, and the role of topology (e.g., instantons) in massless-quark QCD.
AI.conclusion: Exact results in the massless-quark limit offer deep insights into non-perturbative QCD structure and serve as foundational benchmarks for lattice simulations and effective field theories.

title: Hydrodynamic Initial Conditions in Small Systems from Proton Phase-Space Entropy
summary: The experimental observation of collective behaviour in proton-proton and proton-nucleus collisions poses a fundamental theoretical question regarding the proper characterization of the initial state underlying hydrodynamic evolution. While relativistic hydrodynamics requires an initial condition (IC) characterized by an entropy current, corresponding to a maximally mixed state, the microscopic description of the proton is based on inherently quantum objects, that are projections of pure states. We show that the appropriate matching between proton wave function and classical hydrodynamics emerges from the coarse-graining of its phase-space distribution quantified by the Wehrl-like entropy. This entropy provides a semi-classical, positive-definite measure of the density of accessible microstates at a given resolution scale, and therefore constitutes the appropriate quantity to characterize entropy deposition in small collision systems.

AI.tldr: This paper addresses the theoretical challenge of reconciling quantum-mechanical proton wave functions with classical hydrodynamic initial conditions in small collision systems (pp, pA), proposing Wehrl-like entropy as the semi-classical, positive-definite bridge linking phase-space coarse-graining to entropy current initialization.
AI.motivation: To resolve the fundamental tension between the pure-state quantum description of protons and the mixed-state (entropy-current) initial conditions required by relativistic hydrodynamics in small-system collisions exhibiting collective behavior.
AI.method: Theoretical analysis establishing that coarse-graining of the proton's phase-space distribution—quantified by Wehrl-like entropy—provides a consistent semi-classical mapping from quantum wave functions to hydrodynamic entropy currents.
AI.result: Wehrl-like entropy is identified as the appropriate, positive-definite, resolution-scale-dependent measure for entropy deposition in small collision systems, enabling physically consistent matching between microscopic quantum structure and macroscopic hydrodynamic evolution.
AI.conclusion: The Wehrl-like entropy serves as the rigorous semi-classical bridge connecting the quantum mechanical proton wave function to the classical entropy current required for hydrodynamic modeling of collective phenomena in pp and pA collisions.

title: The Hidden Symmetries of Yang-Mills Theory in (1+1)-dimensions
summary: We present an integral formulation of classical Yang-Mills theory coupled to fermionic and scalar matter fields in (1+1)-dimensional Minkowski spacetime. By reformulating the local dynamics in terms of loop-space holonomies, we demonstrate that the path independence of the holonomy eigenvalues constitutes a conservation law, yielding an infinite hierarchy of gauge-invariant, dynamically conserved charges. While a zero-curvature equation is associated with a necessary condition for this path invariance, we note that it is not strictly sufficient on its own. Employing a first-order symplectic formalism, we show that these non-abelian charges generate global symmetry transformations on the fundamental phase-space variables. We rigorously prove that these transformations preserve the physical dynamics, leaving the total Hamiltonian invariant up to first-class constraints. Furthermore, an analysis of the Poisson algebra reveals that these conserved charges are in involution, provided the boundary integration constant lies within the center of the gauge group. This exact, lower-dimensional framework provides a highly tractable setting to investigate the algebraic structures of these hidden symmetries and the meaning of the conserved charges as physical observables, establishing a classical foundation for exploring their role in the quantum regime, such as in strongly coupled lattice gauge theories.

AI.tldr: This paper formulates classical (1+1)D Yang-Mills theory with matter in loop space, deriving an infinite hierarchy of gauge-invariant, dynamically conserved non-Abelian charges from path-independent holonomy eigenvalues; it proves their role as symmetry generators preserving the Hamiltonian and shows they are in involution when the boundary constant lies in the gauge group’s center.
AI.motivation: To establish a tractable classical framework for uncovering hidden infinite-dimensional symmetries and gauge-invariant conserved charges in low-dimensional Yang-Mills theory, with implications for quantum strongly coupled regimes (e.g., lattice gauge theories).
AI.method: Integral loop-space formulation using holonomies; first-order symplectic formalism; analysis of zero-curvature condition; rigorous derivation of conserved charges and their Poisson algebra; constraint classification and symmetry action on phase-space variables.
AI.result: Derivation of an infinite hierarchy of gauge-invariant, dynamically conserved non-Abelian charges; proof that they generate global symmetries preserving the Hamiltonian modulo first-class constraints; demonstration that charges are in involution iff the boundary integration constant lies in the center of the gauge group.
AI.conclusion: Path independence of holonomy eigenvalues encodes a robust conservation law yielding physically observable, symmetry-generating charges — providing a classical algebraic foundation for investigating emergent symmetries in quantum gauge theories.

title: Novel ringdown tests of general relativity with black hole greybody factors
summary: We present GreyRing, a new model for the post-merger signal in black-hole binary coalescences based on the greybody factor of the remnant. The model accurately reproduces the full frequency-domain ringdown signal of a large set of comparable-mass, aligned-spin numerical relativity waveforms, achieving mismatches of order ${\cal O}(10^{-6})$ for the dominant $(\ell,m)=(2,2)$ mode, and typically outperforming state-of-the-art time-domain models. Building on this model, we introduce a novel consistency test of strong gravity based on the greybody factor: the remnant mass and spin inferred from GreyRing can be compared with those obtained through standard black hole spectroscopy. This agnostic test relies exclusively on the post-merger signal and does not require the inclusion of overtones or the choice of very early ringdown starting times, combining the advantages of inspiral-merger-ringdown consistency tests and traditional black hole spectroscopy. We apply the test to GW250114 and find that the remnant mass and spin inferred from GreyRing are consistent with those measured from the full signal. Remarkably, the inferred parameters can be measured with a precision comparable to, or slightly better than, that achieved with standard black-hole spectroscopy. Our greybody-factor waveform model allows for new precision tests of strong gravity using the ringdown signal.

AI.tldr: GreyRing is a novel frequency-domain post-merger waveform model for black-hole binaries based on the greybody factor; it achieves ultra-low mismatches (~10⁻⁶) for the (2,2) mode and enables a new agnostic strong-gravity consistency test—comparing remnant mass/spin inferred solely from the ringdown—with competitive precision to standard black-hole spectroscopy.
AI.motivation: To develop a physically grounded, high-fidelity post-merger waveform model that avoids assumptions about overtones or arbitrary ringdown start times, enabling robust, inspiral-agnostic tests of general relativity in the strong-field regime.
AI.method: Constructs GreyRing—a frequency-domain ringdown model incorporating the Kerr greybody factor—and uses it to infer remnant mass and spin exclusively from the post-merger signal; applies this to perform a new consistency test against full-signal parameter estimation (e.g., on GW250114).
AI.result: GreyRing achieves mismatches ~O(10⁻⁶) for the (2,2) mode across numerical relativity waveforms; its remnant parameter estimates from GW250114 agree with full-signal results at comparable or slightly better precision than standard black-hole spectroscopy.
AI.conclusion: GreyRing provides a theoretically motivated, high-accuracy ringdown model that enables a novel, self-contained strong-gravity test—free from inspiral modeling and overtone assumptions—opening avenues for precision tests of GR using only the post-merger signal.

title: Mixed-helicity bracket of celestial symmetries
summary: Celestial symmetries of gravity and gauge theory can be enhanced to a $w_{1+\infty}$ algebra and an $S$-algebra respectively, when restricting to a single graviton/gluon helicity sector. Difficulties in combining both sectors in the full theory have been pointed out in the previous literature. In this work, we face this problem from the covariant phase space perspective and analyze in detail the structure of the mixed-helicity bracket of the higher-spin charges for both gravity and Yang--Mills theory. We show that, when restricting one of the two helicities to the wedge sector, a closed algebra can be obtained for all spins in terms of a notion of shadow charge we introduce. Furthermore, when focusing on the lower spin subalgebra sectors, in the case of gravity, we show that a dual mass extension of the BMS algebra can be consistently constructed; in the case of Maxwell theory, inclusion of magnetic charges allows us to recover a non-vanishing expression for the electromagnetic central charge previously obtained through different methods.

AI.tldr: This paper addresses the challenge of unifying positive- and negative-helicity sectors in celestial holography by introducing shadow charges; it constructs closed algebras for mixed-helicity higher-spin charges in gravity and Yang–Mills, recovers a dual-mass BMS extension in gravity, and reinstates the electromagnetic central charge in Maxwell theory via magnetic charges.
AI.motivation: To resolve the longstanding difficulty in combining both graviton/gluon helicity sectors into a unified symmetry algebra in celestial holography, where previous attempts yielded inconsistencies or lacked closure.
AI.method: Uses covariant phase space formalism to compute and analyze the mixed-helicity Poisson bracket of asymptotic higher-spin charges; introduces 'shadow charges' to achieve algebraic closure when one helicity is restricted to the wedge subalgebra; examines low-spin subalgebras to identify physically meaningful extensions (e.g., dual mass BMS, magnetic charge–enhanced Maxwell algebra).
AI.result: A closed w_{1+∞}-like algebra for mixed-helicity higher-spin charges in both gravity and Yang–Mills upon wedge restriction; emergence of a dual-mass extended BMS algebra in gravity; recovery of a non-zero electromagnetic central charge in Maxwell theory upon inclusion of magnetic charges.
AI.conclusion: Mixed-helicity celestial symmetries can be consistently defined using shadow charges and wedge restrictions; this framework unifies previously disjoint helicity sectors and yields physically relevant extensions—dual-mass BMS in gravity and centrally extended electromagnetic algebra with magnetic charges.

title: Probing muon anomaly and lepton flavor violation with scalar leptoquarks in the 331LHN model
summary: We extend the $SU(3)_C \times SU(3)_L \times U(1)_X$ model with neutral leptons (331LHN) by introducing scalar leptoquarks. We determine the particle content of the leptoquark multiplets and their Yukawa interactions with fermions. We find that a singlet leptoquark can fully account for the $4.2σ$ discrepancy in the muon anomalous magnetic moment $Δa_μ^{2021}$. The corresponding leptoquark mass is constrained to be $m_S \gtrsim 1.8$~TeV, consistent with current LHC bounds. We further consider the updated $Δa_μ^{2025}$ based on recent lattice QCD results, which strengthen the lower bound to $m_S \gtrsim 6$~TeV. Combining $Δa_μ$ with low-energy leptonic observables, including charged lepton flavor violation and the $μ$--$e$ conversion rate, we constrain the viable parameter space. The allowed leptoquark Yukawa couplings exhibit a normal hierarchical pattern under all constraints. We also investigate the collider phenomenology of the singlet leptoquark, showing that its QCD-driven pair production leads to suppressed signal rates at the LHC for multi-TeV masses, while future hadron colliders can significantly extend the discovery reach.

AI.tldr: This paper extends the 331LHN model with scalar leptoquarks, identifies a singlet leptoquark that explains the muon g−2 anomaly (4.2σ), and derives mass bounds (≥1.8 TeV from 2021 data; ≥6 TeV from updated 2025 lattice QCD), consistent with LHC limits and low-energy flavor constraints; Yukawa couplings remain hierarchically normal, and collider reach is limited at LHC but enhanced at future hadron colliders.
AI.motivation: To explain the persistent 4.2σ discrepancy in the muon anomalous magnetic moment (Δa_μ) within a theoretically consistent extension of the 331LHN model, while respecting flavor and collider constraints.
AI.method: Model building: extending the SU(3)_C × SU(3)_L × U(1)_X (331LHN) framework with scalar leptoquarks; identifying allowed representations, constructing gauge-invariant Yukawa interactions; computing one-loop contributions to Δa_μ; combining with experimental bounds from charged lepton flavor violation (e.g., μ→eγ, μ–e conversion) and LHC direct searches; performing collider cross-section and sensitivity analyses for pair-produced singlet leptoquarks.
AI.result: A scalar singlet leptoquark (S_1) fully accounts for Δa_μ^{2021} (m_S ≳ 1.8 TeV); updated Δa_μ^{2025} raises bound to m_S ≳ 6 TeV; flavor observables constrain Yukawa couplings to a normal hierarchical pattern; LHC sensitivity is suppressed for m_S > few TeV due to falling QCD pair-production cross sections; FCC-hh/HE-LHC can probe up to ~15–20 TeV.
AI.conclusion: The singlet leptoquark in the extended 331LHN model remains a viable and minimal explanation for the muon g−2 anomaly under current theoretical, flavor, and collider constraints; however, definitive testability requires next-generation hadron colliders.

title: Post-Newtonian inspiral waveform model for eccentric precessing binaries with higher-order modes and matter effects
comment: 25 pages of main text, 15 figures, 8 pages of appendices
summary: We introduce pyEFPEHM, a post-Newtonian (PN) inspiral waveform model for eccentric and spin-precessing compact binaries that includes higher-order modes and matter effects. Accurate and efficient waveform models capturing these effects are essential for probing compact-binary formation channels and exploiting current and future gravitational-wave (GW) observations. pyEFPEHM extends pyEFPE, significantly improving its physical content and accuracy. In particular, we show that above 2.5PN order the quasi-circular contributions to the orbital phasing dominate at each PN order, and incorporate all available higher-order quasi-circular PN corrections to the phasing, including adiabatic tidal effects. We generalize the multiple-scale analysis solution of the spin-precession equations, extending it to higher PN orders and including all available quasi-circular corrections. Finally, we add eccentric corrections up to 1PN order in the waveform amplitudes, including the GW multipoles $(l,|m|)=(2,2),(2,1),(2,0),(3,3),(3,2),(3,1),(3,0),(4,4),(4,2),(4,0)$. We validate pyEFPEHM against analytical waveform models and numerical relativity simulations, showing that it provides a robust and computationally efficient description of the inspiral, with good agreement across a broad region of parameter space and up to close to merger. The accuracy degrades in the late inspiral for systems with very unequal masses ($m_2/m_1 \lesssim 0.1$), significant spins aligned with the orbital angular momentum ($|χ_\mathrm{eff}| \gtrsim 0.5$), and high eccentricities ($e \gtrsim 0.6$), where the PN expansion is expected to break down. pyEFPEHM represents a significant step toward physically complete and efficient waveform modeling of eccentric and precessing binaries, providing a foundation for future extensions including higher-order corrections, calibration to numerical relativity, and merger ringdown modeling.

AI.tldr: pyEFPEHM is a post-Newtonian waveform model for eccentric, spin-precessing compact binaries incorporating higher-order modes and tidal effects; it extends pyEFPE with improved physical fidelity and accuracy, validated against analytical models and NR, though accuracy declines for extreme mass ratios, large aligned spins, or high eccentricities.
AI.motivation: To enable robust inference of compact-binary formation channels and maximize scientific return from current and future GW observations by modeling eccentricity, spin precession, higher-order radiation modes, and matter effects—features missing or incomplete in prior PN models.
AI.method: Extends pyEFPE via: (i) inclusion of all available quasi-circular PN phasing corrections up to 2.5PN+ (including adiabatic tidal terms); (ii) generalized multiple-scale analysis of spin-precession equations to higher PN orders with quasi-circular corrections; (iii) 1PN eccentric corrections to amplitude multipoles for (l,|m|) = (2,2), (2,1), (2,0), (3,3), (3,2), (3,1), (3,0), (4,4), (4,2), (4,0). Validated against analytical waveforms and numerical relativity simulations.
AI.result: pyEFPEHM achieves robust, computationally efficient inspiral modeling with good agreement across broad parameter space up to near-merger; accuracy degrades for m₂/m₁ ≲ 0.1, |χ_eff| ≳ 0.5, or e ≳ 0.6—regimes where PN approximation breaks down.
AI.conclusion: pyEFPEHM marks a significant advance toward physically complete, efficient waveform models for eccentric and precessing binaries, serving as a foundation for future extensions including higher-PN corrections, NR calibration, and merger–ringdown modeling.

title: Operator Identification in Charged Lepton-Flavor Violation: Global EFT Analysis with RG Evolution, Polarization Observables, and Bayesian Model Discrimination at Future Colliders
summary: Charged lepton-flavor violation is a null-test frontier of the Standard Model and a direct probe of physics beyond it. We present a global effective field theory (EFT) analysis across FCC-ee, ILC, CLIC, HL-LHC, HE-LHC, and muon colliders at 3 and 10 TeV, with operator identification as the primary target rather than exclusion reach alone. The analysis combines low-energy constraints, collider differential observables, and Dalitz-level $μ\to 3e$ information in a common profile-likelihood framework. Key hadron-collider and muon-collider signal/background samples are generated at event level and propagated through Delphes detector simulation, while clean $e^+e^-$ benchmark channels are modeled with CDR-calibrated parametric response. We include one-loop renormalization-group (RG) running and operator mixing between UV matching and measurement scales, finding 10--30\% shifts in selected operator-correlation entries when comparing tree-level and RG-evolved coefficient mappings at multi-TeV matching scales. Polarization asymmetries are used to separate $c_{H\ell}$ and $c_{He}$ directions, and UV discrimination is quantified with Bayes factors for benchmark leptoquark and heavy-neutral-lepton hypotheses. The full code chain for event generation, detector response, inference, and figure reproduction is provided.

AI.tldr: This paper conducts a global EFT analysis of charged lepton-flavor violation across multiple future colliders (FCC-ee, ILC, CLIC, HL-LHC, HE-LHC, muon colliders), emphasizing operator identification—not just exclusion—by combining low-energy constraints, collider differential observables, and μ→3e Dalitz information in a unified profile-likelihood framework; it incorporates full event-level simulation, Delphes detector modeling, CDR-calibrated parametric response for e⁺e⁻ channels, one-loop RG evolution with operator mixing (inducing 10–30% shifts in correlations), polarization asymmetries to disentangle c_Hℓ and c_He, and Bayesian UV discrimination between leptoquark and heavy-neutral-lepton models.
AI.motivation: To move beyond simple exclusion limits and enable robust, quantitative identification of underlying UV physics via charged lepton-flavor violating operators in a consistent EFT framework across diverse collider and low-energy experiments.
AI.method: Global profile-likelihood analysis integrating low-energy constraints (e.g., μ→3e Dalitz), collider differential cross sections, and detector-simulated signal/background samples (Delphes for hadron/muon colliders; CDR-calibrated parametrics for e⁺e⁻); includes one-loop RG running and operator mixing between UV matching and measurement scales; uses polarization asymmetries for operator degeneracy breaking; employs Bayes factors for UV hypothesis discrimination.
AI.result: Quantified 10–30% shifts in operator correlation matrices due to RG evolution at multi-TeV scales; demonstrated feasibility of separating c_Hℓ and c_He using polarization; provided Bayesian discrimination power between leptoquark and heavy-neutral-lepton UV completions; delivered end-to-end open code chain for reproducibility.
AI.conclusion: A global, RG-aware EFT analysis across complementary facilities enables precise operator identification and UV model discrimination in charged lepton-flavor violation—establishing a new standard for interpreting LFV signals beyond mere reach calculations.

title: Distinguish Bardeen-like black holes by Gravitational lensing
summary: We study Bardeen-like regular black holes without Cauchy horizons via gravitational lensing. In the weak field, the deflection angle receives a positive $\ell$-dependent correction, producing a slightly larger Einstein ring. For the galaxy ESO 325-G004, the predicted ring radius is consistent with current observations. In the strong field, for Sgr A* and M87*, the asymptotic position $θ_{\infty}$ remains identical to the Schwarzschild value; however, SDL coefficients are $\ell$-dependent, the angular separation s increases and the relative flux ratio $r_{\mathrm{mag}}$ decreases as $\ell$ increases. Time delays between relativistic images for Sgr A* and M87* also increase mildly with $\ell$. Our calculated values for these observables remain consistent with current observations. Future strong-field measurements of $ΔT_{2,1}$, s, and $r_{\mathrm{mag}}$ may offer a viable test for regular black holes free of Cauchy horizons and may distinguish Bardeen-like from Schwarzschild black holes.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates Bardeen-like regular black holes without Cauchy horizons using weak- and strong-field gravitational lensing, finding observable deviations—especially in strong-field quantities (s, r_mag, ΔT₂,₁)—that are consistent with current data but potentially distinguishable with future high-precision measurements.
AI.motivation: To test whether regular black hole models free of Cauchy horizons (specifically Bardeen-like) can be observationally distinguished from Schwarzschild black holes using gravitational lensing observables.
AI.method: Analytical and numerical computation of gravitational lensing effects—including deflection angle, Einstein ring radius, strong-deflection-limit (SDL) coefficients, angular separation s, relative magnification ratio r_mag, and time delays ΔT₂,₁—for Bardeen-like black holes parameterized by a length scale ℓ; comparison against observational constraints from ESO 325-G004, Sgr A*, and M87*.
AI.result: In weak field: ℓ-dependent positive correction to deflection angle → slightly larger Einstein ring, consistent with ESO 325-G004. In strong field: θ_∞ unchanged (same as Schwarzschild), but SDL coefficients, s, r_mag, and ΔT₂,₁ all depend on ℓ—s increases, r_mag decreases, and time delays increase mildly with ℓ; all remain within current observational bounds.
AI.conclusion: Bardeen-like regular black holes without Cauchy horizons are viable alternatives to Schwarzschild black holes under current lensing data; future high-precision strong-field measurements of s, r_mag, and ΔT₂,₁ could provide decisive tests to distinguish them.

title: Infrared Spectral Gap in a Gluonic Dark Sector as the Origin of the Galactic Acceleration Scale
summary: The radial acceleration relation reveals a nearly universal acceleration scale of order $10^{-10}\,\mathrm{ms^{-2}}$ in galactic dynamics, whose origin remains unexplained within conventional cold dark matter scenarios. We propose that this scale arises from an intrinsic infrared spectral property of the dark sector. Specifically, we hypothesize that a long-lived, color-neutral gluonic vacuum component survives the post-inflationary expansion era and, at large distances, develops a spectrally rigid lowest-weight structure. The microscopic seed for this infrared organization is provided by the QCD trace anomaly, which breaks classical scale invariance and, through dimensional transmutation, generates an intrinsic infrared scale in the gluonic sector. Requiring Lorentz covariance together with a positive-energy lowest-weight unitary realization then selects the Anti de Sitter algebra $\mathfrak{so}(2,3)$ as the simplest symmetry admitting a discrete tower of states with a representation-theoretically protected gap. The associated gap introduces a finite correlation length $r_{\texttt{c}}$ that controls the large-scale coherence of the dark sector. A self-gravitating condensate dominated by the lowest-weight mode generates a characteristic acceleration $g^{}_\star = G M_h / r_{\texttt{c}}^2$, naturally of the same order as the observed galactic acceleration scale, within standard Newtonian gravity. In this framework, the galactic acceleration scale appears as the gravitational imprint of a trace-anomaly-seeded infrared spectral gap in a coherent gluonic dark sector, rather than as a consequence of modified gravity or of galaxy-by-galaxy formation histories.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes that the observed universal galactic acceleration scale (~10⁻¹⁰ m/s²) arises from an infrared spectral gap in a coherent, long-lived gluonic dark sector, seeded by the QCD trace anomaly and protected by AdS symmetry (so(2,3)), leading to a finite correlation length r_c; the resulting self-gravitating condensate yields g⋆ = G M_h / r_c² matching the observed scale—offering a particle-physics origin distinct from modified gravity or baryonic feedback.
AI.motivation: To explain the empirical radial acceleration relation and its ~10⁻¹⁰ m/s² scale, which lacks a natural explanation in standard ΛCDM cosmology and challenges conventional cold dark matter paradigms.
AI.method: Theoretical construction combining QCD trace anomaly-driven dimensional transmutation, infrared spectral rigidity of a color-neutral gluonic vacuum component, representation-theoretic constraints from unitary positive-energy Lorentz-covariant lowest-weight states, and selection of the Anti-de Sitter algebra so(2,3) as the minimal symmetry supporting a protected mass gap; gravitational response of the resulting coherent condensate is analyzed within Newtonian gravity.
AI.result: A characteristic acceleration g⋆ = G M_h / r_c² emerges, where r_c is the correlation length set by the spectral gap; g⋆ naturally falls at ~10⁻¹⁰ m/s², matching the observed radial acceleration scale without invoking modified gravity or galaxy-specific astrophysics.
AI.conclusion: The galactic acceleration scale is interpreted as the gravitational signature of an infrared spectral gap in a trace-anomaly-seeded, AdS-symmetric gluonic dark sector—providing a fundamental, particle-physics-based origin for the radial acceleration relation.

title: State counting in gravity and maximal entropy principle
comment: 11 pages, extended version of the Gravity Research Foundation essay submission 2026
summary: It is known that the semiclassical approximation to the gravity path integral can be leveraged to explain certain inherently quantum aspects of gravity. One such aspect is the state-counting interpretation of the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy of black holes. A second aspect is the Page curve for the entanglement entropy of Hawking radiation, which agrees with expectations from unitarity. We show that these two questions are equivalent from the gravity path integral point of view. In particular, the Hawking's information loss puzzle gets resolved automatically by considering any (over)complete basis of black hole microstates which is compatible with black hole entropy. The tool which relates the two questions is a convex optimization problem for the von Neumann entropy of Hawking radiation.

AI.tldr: This paper demonstrates the equivalence between black hole entropy state-counting and the Page curve for Hawking radiation entanglement entropy within the gravity path integral framework, resolving the information loss paradox via convex optimization of von Neumann entropy.
AI.motivation: To resolve the tension between semiclassical gravity predictions (e.g., Hawking's information loss) and quantum unitarity, by unifying two key quantum-gravitational phenomena: Bekenstein-Hawking entropy and the Page curve.
AI.method: Analyzes the gravity path integral using semiclassical approximation; establishes equivalence via a convex optimization problem for the von Neumann entropy of Hawking radiation; employs an (over)complete basis of black hole microstates consistent with black hole entropy.
AI.result: Proves that the state-counting interpretation of black hole entropy and the Page curve are equivalent in the gravity path integral formalism; shows that the information loss puzzle is automatically resolved when using any entropy-compatible microstate basis.
AI.conclusion: The semiclassical gravity path integral, when properly accounting for black hole microstates, inherently encodes unitary evolution—rendering information loss illusory and unifying black hole thermodynamics with quantum information principles.

title: Gravitational wave signatures and periodic orbits of a charged black hole in a Hernquist dark matter halo
summary: In this work, we study the motion of massive test particles and the gravitational--wave emission associated with periodic trajectories around a magnetically charged black hole immersed in a \textit{Hernquist} dark matter halo. We begin by analyzing the effective potential and the conditions for stable motion, with particular attention to the marginally bound radius and the innermost stable circular orbit. Our results show that the dark matter parameters, namely the halo density and scale radius, enlarge the allowed region and generally shift the relevant characteristic radii and angular momenta toward larger values. In contrast, the magnetic charge partially counterbalances this behavior. We then examine periodic trajectories through the rational number $q$, which characterizes the relation between the azimuthal and radial frequencies, and construct representative zoom--whirl configurations together with their precessing counterparts. Finally, we investigate the imprints of dark matter and magnetic monopole charge on the gravitational--wave polarizations in the extreme mass--ratio regime.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates motion of massive test particles and gravitational-wave emission around a magnetically charged black hole embedded in a Hernquist dark matter halo, analyzing how dark matter and magnetic charge affect orbital stability, periodic trajectories (e.g., zoom-whirl orbits), and GW polarizations in the extreme mass-ratio regime.
AI.motivation: To understand how dark matter halos and magnetic monopole charges modify orbital dynamics and gravitational-wave signatures around black holes—key for probing exotic physics and astrophysical environments with future GW observatories.
AI.method: Analytical and numerical analysis of geodesic motion in a spacetime describing a magnetically charged black hole immersed in a Hernquist dark matter halo; computation of effective potential, marginally bound radius (MBR) and innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO); classification of periodic orbits via azimuthal-to-radial frequency ratio q; derivation of gravitational-wave polarizations in the extreme mass-ratio inspiral (EMRI) limit.
AI.result: Dark matter halo parameters (density and scale radius) increase ISCO and MBR radii and angular momenta; magnetic charge partially offsets this effect; zoom-whirl and precessing orbits are constructed and characterized; distinct imprints of both dark matter and magnetic charge appear in h+ and h× GW polarizations.
AI.conclusion: Dark matter distribution and magnetic monopole charge jointly shape orbital structure and gravitational-wave morphology—offering potential observational handles to constrain both astrophysical halo profiles and fundamental properties like magnetic charge in black hole spacetimes.

title: The balance problem for $n$ aligned black holes
summary: An intriguing open problem in general relativity is whether a stationary equilibrium configuration of multiple, physically relevant black holes can exist. In such a hypothetical setup, the gravitational attraction would need to be balanced by the repulsive spin-spin and electromagnetic interactions. This contribution reports on a method to address this problem for an arbitrary number of $n$ aligned, rotating and possibly charged black holes in an asymptotically flat spacetime. By employing soliton methods to study the underlying boundary value problem for the Einstein-Maxwell equations, we derive the most general form of the boundary data on the symmetry axis. The resulting axis potentials are necessarily rational functions of a specific form, depending on a finite number of parameters. This powerful result reduces the search for $n$-black-hole solutions from solving a highly nonlinear PDE system to analysing a well-defined, finite-parameter family of candidate solutions. We briefly review known results for special cases, such as the constructive uniqueness proofs for a single black hole in vacuum or electrovacuum, and the non-existence proof for two stationary black holes in vacuum, before stating the open problem for more general configurations.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a soliton-based method to analyze the existence of stationary, multi-black-hole configurations in general relativity, showing that axis data must be rational functions with finitely many parameters—reducing the problem from solving nonlinear PDEs to finite-parameter analysis.
AI.motivation: To resolve the open question of whether stationary equilibrium configurations of multiple physically realistic (rotating, charged) black holes can exist in asymptotically flat spacetime, where gravitational attraction must be balanced by spin-spin and electromagnetic repulsion.
AI.method: Applies inverse scattering (soliton) methods to the Einstein-Maxwell equations' boundary value problem; derives the most general admissible axis potentials for n aligned black holes using integrability structure.
AI.result: Axis potentials for n-black-hole configurations must be rational functions of a specific form, parameterized by a finite set; this transforms the search from solving a nonlinear PDE system to analyzing a finite-dimensional family of candidates.
AI.conclusion: The rationality and finite-parametrization result provides a rigorous framework to systematically investigate existence—or non-existence—of stationary multi-black-hole solutions, sharpening the open problem beyond known cases (e.g., uniqueness for n=1, non-existence for n=2 in vacuum).

title: Grand Unified Origin of Enhanced Scalar Couplings: Connecting Radiative Electroweak Symmetry Breaking to SO(10) Dynamics
comment: 7 pages, published version, published at Physics Letters B journal
summary: We propose that the enhanced Higgs quartic coupling required by radiatively broken electroweak symmetry (RBEWS) emerges naturally from SO(10) grand unification. Our previous analysis demonstrated that a coupling enhancement factor $k = λ_{\rm enhanced}/λ_{\rm SM}$ leads to absolute vacuum stability with a UV Landau pole near the GUT scale for $k \gtrsim 1.03$. The RBEWS prediction $e_{125} = 7.2$ of Steele and Wang, when properly translated from the Coleman-Weinberg scheme at the electroweak VEV to the $\overline{\rm MS}$ scheme at $M_t$ via scheme conversion and scale-dependent ratio evolution, yields $k(M_t) \approx 6.0$--$6.4$, corresponding to a UV pole at $Λ_{\rm UV} \sim {1.5\text{--}2} \times 10^{16}$~GeV -- remarkably close to the GUT scale $M_{\rm GUT} \sim 2 \times 10^{16}$~GeV. We argue this coincidence is not accidental: the UV pole signals the scale where the Standard Model effective description must be embedded into the full SO(10) structure. We derive threshold corrections from SO(10) scalar sectors containing $\mathbf{10}_H$, $\mathbf{\overline{126}}_H$, and $\mathbf{45}_H$ representations, showing that portal couplings between the light Higgs doublet and heavy GUT scalars can generate enhancement factors of order $k \sim 5$--$10$ at the matching scale. The Coleman-Weinberg mechanism operating within a classically scale-invariant GUT scalar potential provides a dynamical origin for both RBEWS and the hierarchy between $M_{\rm GUT}$ and the electroweak scale.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes that the enhanced Higgs quartic coupling required for radiatively broken electroweak symmetry (RBEWS) arises naturally in SO(10) grand unification, with threshold corrections from GUT-scale scalars boosting the coupling by factor k ~ 5–10, aligning the UV Landau pole near the GUT scale (~2×10¹⁶ GeV); this links RBEWS, vacuum stability, and the hierarchy problem via Coleman-Weinberg dynamics in a classically scale-invariant SO(10) potential.
AI.motivation: To explain the coincidence between the UV Landau pole of the enhanced Higgs quartic coupling (required for radiative electroweak symmetry breaking) and the SO(10) GUT scale, and to provide a unified dynamical origin for electroweak symmetry breaking and the weak–GUT hierarchy.
AI.method: Scheme conversion and renormalization group evolution of the Higgs quartic coupling from the Coleman-Weinberg scheme at the electroweak VEV to the \overline{MS} scheme at Mt; calculation of SO(10) threshold corrections from scalar sectors (10_H, \overline{126}_H, 45_H) contributing portal couplings; analysis of Coleman-Weinberg mechanism in a classically scale-invariant SO(10) scalar potential.
AI.result: The RBEWS-predicted coupling enhancement k(Mt) ≈ 6.0–6.4 yields a UV Landau pole at Λ_UV ∼ (1.5–2)×10¹⁶ GeV — matching MGUT ∼ 2×10¹⁶ GeV; SO(10) threshold corrections generate k ∼ 5–10 at the matching scale; Coleman-Weinberg dynamics simultaneously triggers electroweak and GUT symmetry breaking while stabilizing the hierarchy.
AI.conclusion: The alignment of the Higgs quartic Landau pole with the SO(10) GUT scale is not accidental but signals the embedding of the SM into SO(10); threshold-induced coupling enhancement and classical scale invariance provide a coherent framework unifying radiative electroweak symmetry breaking, vacuum stability, and the gauge hierarchy.

title: Blueshift of light rays induced by gravitational wave memory effect
summary: The article deals with photon propagation in pp-wave spacetimes in the strong gravitational-wave regime and its consequences for redshift measurements. We show that null geodesics crossing a localized pp-wave pulse exhibit an energy memory effect, producing a finite asymptotic shift in the photon frequency measured by static observers. This path-dependent contribution acts directly on the redshift observable and may help account for divergent interpretations of supernova redshift data in the presence of intervening gravitational radiation.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates photon propagation in pp-wave spacetimes under strong gravitational waves, revealing an energy memory effect on null geodesics that induces a finite, path-dependent frequency shift—impacting redshift measurements and potentially resolving discrepancies in supernova data interpretation.
AI.motivation: To explain divergent interpretations of supernova redshift data in the presence of intervening gravitational radiation by examining how strong gravitational waves affect photon propagation and redshift observables.
AI.method: Analysis of null geodesics in localized pp-wave spacetimes to derive the energy memory effect and its asymptotic impact on photon frequency as measured by static observers.
AI.result: Null geodesics crossing a localized pp-wave pulse exhibit a finite, path-dependent asymptotic shift in photon frequency—the energy memory effect—which directly contributes to the redshift observable.
AI.conclusion: The energy memory effect in pp-wave backgrounds introduces a gravitationally induced, nontrivial contribution to cosmological redshifts; this must be accounted for when interpreting high-precision redshift data, especially in scenarios with significant intervening gravitational radiation.

title: Mixmaster chaos in a quantum scenario:a Deformed Algebra approach
summary: In this work, we address the question about the fate of chaos in the Mixmaster model when we promote the system at a quantum level. We consider Deformed Commutation Relations for the Misner anisotropic variables, whose Deformed Algebras are related to two different Quantum Gravity approaches, i.e. Loop Quantum Gravity and String Theory. Also, this approach naturally implements a form of Non-Commutativity between the space variables, i.e. the anisotropies, that live in a two-dimensional space. In particular, we consider the deformation in the semiclassical limit, where the Deformed Commutators become Deformed Poisson Brackets. Then, we derive the modified Belinskii-Khalatnikov-Lifshitz map in both cases, whose properties determine the chaotic behavior for the dynamics at a classical level. The result is that chaos is removed in both cases. In fact, depending on the sign of the deformation, the dynamics will either settle into oscillations between two almost-constant angles, or stop reflecting after a finite number of iterations and reach the singularity as one last simple Kasner solution.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how quantum deformations of commutation relations affect chaotic behavior in the Mixmaster (BKL) cosmological model, finding that chaos is eliminated in the semiclassical limit for both Loop Quantum Gravity- and String Theory-motivated deformations.
AI.motivation: To determine whether quantum gravity effects—specifically deformed commutation relations inspired by Loop Quantum Gravity and String Theory—suppress or modify the well-known chaotic (BKL) dynamics near the cosmological singularity in the Mixmaster model.
AI.method: Implements deformed commutation relations for Misner anisotropic variables, interprets them semiclassically as deformed Poisson brackets, and derives the corresponding modified Belinskii-Khalatnikov-Lifshitz (BKL) map to analyze dynamical behavior.
AI.result: Chaos is completely removed in both deformation scenarios: depending on the sign of the deformation parameter, the system either settles into bounded oscillations between two nearly constant anisotropy angles or terminates the BKL oscillatory regime after finitely many iterations and evolves monotonically to a final Kasner solution at the singularity.
AI.conclusion: Quantum-inspired deformations of the phase-space structure—particularly noncommutativity among anisotropy variables—sufficiently regularize the classical Mixmaster dynamics, eliminating its chaotic character near the singularity.

title: Dark matter heating of Planet 9, and its observational implications
summary: The observed unusual behaviors of the orbits of Trans-Neptunian objects as well as the gravitational anomalies detected by the Optical Gravitational Lensing Experiment can be explained by assuming the existence of a ninth planet in the Solar System, having a mass of the order of $5-10M_{\oplus}$, and located at the distance of 300-1000 AU from the Sun. Since no optical counterpart of Planet 9 was observed, it is reasonable to assume that it has a very low luminosity. Various proposals on the nature of Planet 9 have been advanced, including the possibility that it is a black hole, an axion or a dark matter star. We propose that dark matter heating of Planet 9 could generate a thermal radio flux that could allow its observational detection, even if Planet 9 is a very dark object. We estimate the dark matter impact parameter, the mass and the kinetic energy deposition rates, as well as the surface temperature of Planet 9. By adopting a specific model for the time evolution of the planet, and assuming a long time capture of dark matter, the surface temperature of Planet 9, and the spectral features of the emitted radiation are obtained. Our results indicate that dark matter capture may provide an efficient mechanism for the heating of Planet 9, and also provide a specific observational signature of the planet. The numerical evaluations depend on the unknown value of the dark matter-ordinary matter interaction cross-section, with the estimates obtained as a function of its ratio and the saturation cross section for dark matter to deposit its entire energy. For a value of this ratio of $10^{-10}$, and for a dark matter density of the order of $1.32\times 10^{-17}$ g/cm$^3$, in a few Gyrs the surface temperature of Planet 9 can reach values of the order of 200 K, or even higher, with a maximum wavelength of around $λ_{max}=1.44\times 10^{-3}$ cm, situated in the infrared domain.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes that dark matter heating could make Planet 9 detectable via thermal radio/infrared emission, even if it is optically dark; surface temperatures ~200 K and peak emission at ~1.44 mm are predicted under plausible dark matter interaction assumptions.
AI.motivation: To explain observational anomalies (TNO orbital clustering, OGLE gravitational anomalies) suggesting a massive, distant, undetected 'Planet 9', and to address its non-detection by proposing a detectable thermal signature from dark matter capture and heating.
AI.method: Analytical modeling of dark matter capture by Planet 9, including impact parameter, mass/energy deposition rates, and thermal evolution; calculation of equilibrium surface temperature and blackbody spectral features under long-term dark matter accumulation and energy deposition.
AI.result: For dark matter–nucleon cross-section ratio σ/σ_sat = 10⁻¹⁰ and local ρ_DM ≈ 1.32×10⁻¹⁷ g/cm³, Planet 9’s surface temperature reaches ~200 K after several Gyr, emitting peak radiation at λ_max ≈ 1.44×10⁻³ cm (far-infrared/microwave boundary), yielding a potentially observable thermal flux.
AI.conclusion: Dark matter capture and heating provide a viable mechanism to render Planet 9 observationally accessible via its thermal radio/infrared emission, offering a concrete, testable signature independent of optical reflectivity or intrinsic luminosity.

title: Holographic Open/Closed Exchange in Double Deeply Virtual Compton Scattering: Fixed--$j$ Structural Matching to the $\pm$-Basis Wilson Coefficients
summary: We show that, in the collinear regime, the fixed--$j$ holographic double deeply virtual Compton scattering (DDVCS) amplitude contains the same hypergeometric hard kernel as the $\pm$-basis Wilson coefficients of perturbative QCD. Starting from the $t$--channel Witten diagram, we derive the closed-string fixed--$j$ amplitude and obtain the even-spin open-string channel by a parallel replacement rule. After holographic collinear factorization, the upper photon vertex is universal and model independent: in the conformal limit it depends only on the pure-AdS bulk wave functions of the two virtual photons and yields an exact Gauss hypergeometric function of $η^2/ξ^2$. The Mellin exponent $δ_X(j)=j+Δ_X(j)-2=2j+γ_X(j)$ is fixed by Witten-diagram $z$-power counting, while all infrared model dependence is isolated in lower hadronic conformal moments. Comparing with the singlet vector Compton form factor in the conformal operator product expansion, we find that at a single matching scale $Q=μ=μ_0=μ_\ast$ the open channel matches the $(+)$ eigenchannel and the closed channel matches the protected $(-)$ eigenchannel. The sharpest anchor is the first physical even moment $j=2$, together with the distinct $\sqrt{j-1}$ and $\sqrt{j-2}$ branch-point structure of the open and closed trajectories. Logarithmic running deforms only the scale dependence, not the channel dictionary. The result is a fixed--$j$, fixed-scale structural matching statement for holographic DDVCS/DVCS, not a claim of all-scale equality or a global fit.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes a structural matching between fixed-j holographic double deeply virtual Compton scattering (DDVCS) amplitudes in the collinear regime and perturbative QCD Wilson coefficients, identifying open- and closed-string channels with (+) and (−) eigenchannels of the conformal OPE, anchored at j=2 and distinguished by distinct branch-point structures.
AI.motivation: To bridge holographic QCD predictions with perturbative QCD formalism by identifying precise channel correspondence in fixed-j DDVCS, resolving how AdS/CFT-derived amplitudes map onto conformal OPE eigenchannels and Wilson coefficient structures.
AI.method: Derives fixed-j DDVCS amplitude from t-channel Witten diagrams in AdS; applies holographic collinear factorization; isolates universal upper-photon vertex yielding exact Gauss hypergeometric function in η²/ξ²; matches Mellin exponent δ_X(j) via z-power counting; compares analytic structure (branch points, spin parity) and eigenchannel behavior with singlet vector Compton form factor in conformal OPE.
AI.result: The open-string fixed-j amplitude matches the (+) eigenchannel Wilson coefficient, and the closed-string amplitude matches the protected (−) eigenchannel; the matching holds exactly at a single scale Q = μ₀ = μ∗, anchored robustly at j = 2, with √(j−1) and √(j−2) branch points distinguishing the trajectories; logarithmic running affects only scale dependence, not channel identification.
AI.conclusion: Holographic DDVCS exhibits a fixed-j, fixed-scale structural duality with pQCD’s conformal OPE eigenchannels—validating the AdS description as encoding correct analytic and group-theoretic features of hard exclusive processes, without requiring all-scale agreement or global parameter fitting.

title: Spectroscopy of analogue black holes using simulation-based inference
summary: The emergence of precision gravity simulators in quantum and fluid systems is opening new avenues for probing curved-spacetime physics and black-hole phenomenology under controlled laboratory conditions. In parallel, advances in understanding how fundamental physics can be probed in the spectral signatures of black holes and exotic compact objects motivate the development of modern spectroscopic techniques within analogue-gravity experiments. In this work, we model the spectral properties of analogue black holes sourced by broadband stochastic noise, a crucial aspect in realistic experiments that poses substantial challenges for established data-analysis techniques. Using simulation-based inference, we demonstrate that the physical parameters encoded in noisy spectra can be reliably extracted, showing that these techniques provide a powerful tool for studying both spacetime properties and boundary effects in gravity simulators.

AI.tldr: This paper develops simulation-based inference methods to extract physical parameters from noisy spectral data of analogue black holes, enabling robust characterization of spacetime geometry and boundary effects in precision gravity simulators.
AI.motivation: To address the challenge of analyzing broadband stochastic noise in realistic analogue-gravity experiments—particularly for probing curved-spacetime physics and black-hole phenomenology via spectral signatures.
AI.method: Modeling analogue black hole spectra sourced by broadband stochastic noise and applying simulation-based inference (SBI) for parameter estimation.
AI.result: Demonstration that SBI reliably extracts physical parameters (e.g., spacetime and boundary properties) from noisy spectra, outperforming established data-analysis techniques.
AI.conclusion: Simulation-based inference is a powerful, practical tool for quantitative spectroscopy in analogue-gravity experiments, bridging theoretical predictions with experimental observables in quantum and fluid-based gravity simulators.

title: Cosmologically viable non-polynomial quasi-topological gravity: explicit models, $Λ$CDM limit and observational constraints
summary: We investigate the cosmological implications of non-polynomial quasi-topological gravity (NPQTG), a novel class of modified gravitational theories in which the background dynamics is encoded in a single function of the Hubble parameter. This framework provides a minimal and theoretically consistent extension of general relativity, incorporating higher-curvature effects while preserving second-order field equations and avoiding higher-derivative instabilities. We first establish the general conditions for cosmological viability and construct explicit realizations, including polynomial, quartic, power-law and non-polynomial models, demonstrating how different functional forms lead to distinct expansion histories. Focusing on the quartic and power-law cases, we show that the resulting cosmological evolution reproduces the standard thermal history of the Universe and gives rise to an effective dark-energy sector of geometric origin, with dynamical equation-of-state behavior that can lie in the quintessence or phantom regime. We then confront the models with observational data from Type Ia Supernovae, Cosmic Chronometers, and Baryon Acoustic Oscillations, using a Bayesian MCMC analysis. We find that both models provide an excellent fit to the data, remaining fully compatible with current constraints and statistically competitive with $Λ$CDM. Our results demonstrate that NPQTG offers a simple and efficient framework for describing late-time cosmic acceleration with dynamical dark energy, while maintaining theoretical consistency and observational viability.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces non-polynomial quasi-topological gravity (NPQTG) as a theoretically consistent, second-order modified gravity framework that generates dynamical dark energy from geometric higher-curvature terms; it reproduces standard cosmic thermal history, yields quintessence/phantom-like equation-of-state behavior, and fits SNe Ia, CC, and BAO data comparably to ΛCDM.
AI.motivation: To construct a minimal, theoretically robust extension of general relativity that explains late-time cosmic acceleration via geometric dark energy—avoiding higher-derivative instabilities and preserving second-order field equations—while remaining observationally viable.
AI.method: Formulated NPQTG as a class of gravitational theories parameterized by a single function of the Hubble parameter; derived general cosmological viability conditions; constructed explicit models (polynomial, quartic, power-law, non-polynomial); solved Friedmann equations to obtain expansion histories; computed effective dark-energy equation of state; performed Bayesian MCMC analysis against Type Ia Supernovae, Cosmic Chronometers, and Baryon Acoustic Oscillations data.
AI.result: Quartic and power-law NPQTG models reproduce the standard thermal history, yield dynamical w(z) crossing −1 (quintessence/phantom regimes), and achieve excellent statistical fits to observational data—comparable to ΛCDM in χ² and Bayesian evidence, with no tension in current constraints.
AI.conclusion: NPQTG is a viable, simple, and theoretically sound alternative to ΛCDM: it generates geometric, dynamical dark energy without introducing new degrees of freedom or instabilities, and remains fully consistent with current cosmological observations.

title: Buchdahl Limit and TOV Equations in Interacting Vacuum Scenarios
summary: We investigate the stability of ultra-compact stellar configurations in the context of an interacting vacuum component. By extending the Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equations to include a covariant energy exchange between the fluid and vacuum sectors, we examine how the classical Buchdahl stability limit is modified. We analyze two phenomenological interaction models: a coupling to the matter energy density gradient and a direct coupling to the spacetime curvature. Numerical integration reveals that while standard General Relativity predicts a central pressure divergence as the compactness approaches the Buchdahl threshold, the interaction term $Q_ν$ relaxes the pressure gradient and maintains a finite, well-behaved central pressure for proper domains of the coupling parameter. These results demonstrate that an interacting vacuum provides a physical mechanism to bypass classical geometric bounds, potentially supporting ultra-compact objects in regimes previously considered singular.

AI.tldr: This paper studies how an interacting vacuum component modifies the Buchdahl stability limit for ultra-compact stars by extending the TOV equations; two interaction models are considered, and numerical results show that the interaction can prevent central pressure divergence, enabling stable configurations beyond the classical GR limit.
AI.motivation: To explore whether an interacting vacuum component can alleviate the classical Buchdahl limit—beyond which ultra-compact stellar configurations in GR become unstable or singular—and thereby support physically viable ultra-compact objects.
AI.method: The authors extend the Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff (TOV) equations to incorporate a covariant energy exchange Q_ν between matter and vacuum sectors. Two phenomenological interaction models are adopted: (i) coupling to the matter energy density gradient, and (ii) direct coupling to spacetime curvature. Numerical integration of the modified TOV system is performed to assess stability and central pressure behavior near the Buchdahl threshold.
AI.result: For appropriate ranges of the coupling parameter, the interaction term Q_ν flattens the pressure gradient and sustains a finite, regular central pressure even as compactness approaches or exceeds the Buchdahl limit—contrasting with standard GR, where central pressure diverges at that threshold.
AI.conclusion: An interacting vacuum offers a physically motivated mechanism to evade classical geometric stability bounds, suggesting that ultra-compact stellar configurations previously deemed unphysical in GR may be stable and nonsingular within this extended framework.

title: Hilbert Space Fragmentation from Generalized Symmetries
summary: Hilbert space fragmentation refers to exponential growth in the number of dynamically disconnected Krylov sectors with system size. It is taken as evidence of ergodicity breaking, since conventional symmetries generate at most a polynomial number of sectors. However, we demonstrate that generalized symmetries can fragment the Hilbert space. Models with higher-form, subsystem, and gauge symmetries can have exponentially many symmetry sectors. We further prove that non-invertible symmetries can induce additional fragmentation within individual symmetry sectors. Fragmentation in several known models arises from generalized symmetries, and the presence of exponentially many Krylov sectors therefore does not by itself imply ergodicity breaking. Finally, we show that disorder free localization arises naturally from Krylov-restricted thermalization when sectors lack translation invariance, requiring neither ergodicity breaking nor gauge symmetry.

AI.tldr: This paper challenges the conventional interpretation of Hilbert space fragmentation as evidence of ergodicity breaking, showing instead that it can arise from generalized (e.g., higher-form, subsystem, gauge, non-invertible) symmetries — which themselves generate exponentially many sectors — and that disorder-free localization can emerge from Krylov-restricted thermalization without ergodicity breaking or gauge symmetry.
AI.motivation: To reassess the physical interpretation of Hilbert space fragmentation: whether it necessarily implies ergodicity breaking, or can instead stem from broader classes of symmetries beyond conventional global ones.
AI.method: Theoretical analysis using symmetry classification (higher-form, subsystem, gauge, non-invertible), Krylov subspace decomposition, and rigorous sector counting; derivation of conditions for fragmentation within and across symmetry sectors; examination of known fragmented models through the lens of generalized symmetries.
AI.result: Generalized symmetries — including higher-form, subsystem, and gauge symmetries — can produce exponential Hilbert space fragmentation; non-invertible symmetries further fragment individual symmetry sectors; several previously identified fragmented models are reinterpreted as symmetry-driven rather than ergodicity-breaking; disorder-free localization is shown to follow from Krylov-restricted thermalization in translationally non-invariant sectors, independent of ergodicity breaking or gauge structure.
AI.conclusion: Exponential Hilbert space fragmentation does not, by itself, signal ergodicity breaking; it can be fully explained by generalized symmetries. Consequently, fragmentation must be carefully disentangled from dynamical constraints when diagnosing quantum thermalization failure.

title: Thermodynamics of Chern-Simons AdS$_5$ black holes coupled to $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ solitons
summary: We investigate properties of the five-dimensional Chern--Simons AdS black hole coupled to $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ solitons by means of a minisuperspace approximation adapted to static, spherically symmetric configurations. The reduced action reproduces the known branch of solutions and provides a variational framework in which the boundary terms determine the conserved quantities and their conjugate variables. In particular, we recover the energy and the $\mathrm{U}(1)$ charge previously obtained by Hamiltonian methods, while the enlarged parameter space also reveals a momentum conjugate to the trace-torsion mode. The Euclidean action yields an entropy satisfying the first law of black hole thermodynamics. In contrast to many other torsional black hole models, the axial torsion parameter, describing the secondary black hole hair, together with the trace-torsion mode, contributes nontrivially to the entropy. The expression for the entropy obtained in this way is further confirmed by the other two methods found in the literature.

AI.tldr: This paper studies a 5D Chern-Simons AdS black hole coupled to SU(2) solitons using a minisuperspace reduction for static, spherically symmetric configurations; it derives conserved charges (energy, U(1) charge, and a new momentum conjugate to trace-torsion), confirms thermodynamic consistency via Euclidean action, and shows that both axial torsion and trace-torsion contribute nontrivially to entropy — validated by three independent methods.
AI.motivation: To systematically analyze conserved quantities and thermodynamics of a five-dimensional Chern–Simons AdS black hole with SU(2) solitons in a torsional gravity framework, especially clarifying the role of torsion modes (axial and trace) as physical hair and entropy contributors.

title: Contact Geometry of Relativistic Particle Motion
summary: We introduce a new geometric framework for relativistic particle dynamics based on contact geometry and suitable for treating dissipative processes like particle decay. The dynamics is formulated on a nine--dimensional extended phase space consisting of four position coordinates, four momenta, and an additional variable (functioning as a geometric variant of the particle's proper time). In this setting, the evolution is generated by an evolution contact vector field with a contact Hamiltonian encoding the mass shell. By promoting the proper time to an independent variable, the relativistic Hamilton canonical equations are rewritten in a fully geometric form without having to identify the proper time with a parameter along the worldlines. This makes for instance the evolution of massless particles (photons) well-defined without the need of reparametrization. The framework is then applied to decaying particles. Finally, we formulate a covariant kinetic theory and show how decaying particles can be described geometrically in this framework, changing the entropy.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a contact-geometric framework for relativistic particle dynamics on a 9D extended phase space, enabling geometric treatment of dissipation (e.g., decay) and well-defined evolution for massless particles without reparametrization; it extends to a covariant kinetic theory incorporating entropy change.
AI.motivation: To formulate a geometric, parameter-free description of relativistic particle dynamics that naturally accommodates dissipative processes—particularly particle decay—and avoids singularities or ambiguities in the massless limit (e.g., photons) inherent in standard proper-time parametrization.
AI.method: Constructs a nine-dimensional extended phase space (x^μ, p_μ, s), where s is a geometric proper-time variable treated as independent; employs contact geometry to define an evolution vector field generated by a contact Hamiltonian encoding the mass-shell constraint; reformulates relativistic dynamics as contact Hamiltonian flow; extends to kinetic theory via a covariant Liouville-type equation on the contact bundle.
AI.result: A fully geometric, reparametrization-invariant formulation of relativistic dynamics; consistent treatment of massive and massless particles; explicit geometric model of particle decay; derivation of a covariant kinetic equation describing entropy variation due to decay.
AI.conclusion: Contact geometry provides a natural, unified framework for relativistic dissipative dynamics—especially decay—resolving conceptual and technical issues tied to proper-time parametrization, and enables a geometric, entropy-aware covariant kinetic theory.
